sections.heading: Starting with an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali East
paragraphs: Have four things ready and the first session will be worth double. The most recent report card or criterion sheet, including the teacher comments nobody reads. Two or three returned pieces of work with the marks still on them, ideally one bad one. The student's actual weekly timetable, including the sport, the music class and the tuition you already run, so the slot we agree is a slot that exists. And one sentence from you on what you want different in three months, written down before the call.

The first session is a diagnostic, and it should feel like one. The tutor works backwards from the returned papers to find where the method actually breaks, rather than starting at the top of the syllabus. For a Diploma Programme student that usually means opening the Internal Assessment draft or the mark scheme from the last test. For an IGCSE student it often means a single past-paper question taken slowly, with the mark scheme visible, so the student sees for the first time that marks have locations. The tutor talks less than you expect and asks more.

Afterwards you get a short written note: what the student can do unaided, the two or three specific gaps, what the next four weeks will cover and in what order. That note is the thing to hold the arrangement against. If the second month does not look like the note, the note was wrong and we will say so. For families looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai, this is the part that tends to be missing: not the teaching, but the written account of what the teaching is for.

Timing, finally. If you are reading this in June or July, start now, because the problem you are about to have in October is cheaper to fix in July. If you are reading it in January with a Year 2 Diploma Programme student, say so in the first message and we will match for triage rather than for the long build: a tutor who will pick the two papers where marks are most recoverable and work those hard. Either way, tell us the month you are in. It changes the shortlist.

faqs.question: How quickly can home classes start in Kandivali East?
faqs.answer: Usually within three to five days for mainstream subjects, because several tutors already work inside Thakur Complex and the surrounding lanes. You get the shortlist within a day or two of sending the details, you speak to the tutors, and the first diagnostic session is scheduled after you choose. Scarce Higher Level subjects such as HL Economics or HL Computer Science take longer, sometimes a fortnight, and we will tell you that upfront rather than filling the slot with someone who does not teach the syllabus. If the timing is tight because an Internal Assessment deadline is close, say so in the first message and we prioritise accordingly.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Kandivali East depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then subject scarcity, session length, frequency and travel distance. Diploma Programme Higher Level costs more than IGCSE Core because the pool of people who can teach it well is smaller. A subject where only a handful of tutors in Mumbai are genuinely competent costs more again. Internal Assessment supervision alongside regular syllabus teaching is more work and prices accordingly. Travel matters less in this township than almost anywhere else this far north, because short internal distances mean a tutor is not absorbing an hour of highway per family. We do not publish a rate card; you get a written quote for your specific subject and level before anything is booked.

faqs.question: Will a tutor get past the gate at my building in Thakur Complex?
faqs.answer: Yes, but set it up in the first week rather than the third. Most buildings here run a visitor register or a resident-approved entry list, and the smooth version is that you add the tutor as a standing weekly visitor with the security desk, giving the name, phone number and the arrival window. The friction version is the tutor being phoned up from the gate every week, which costs five to ten minutes each time and eventually costs punctuality. Tell us the lane, the building name and the nearest landmark when the match is made, because internal township addresses do not always resolve cleanly on a mapping app.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For a younger PYP or MYP student, yes, someone should be in the flat, though not in the room. For an IGCSE or Diploma Programme student it is not necessary after the first two or three sessions, and hovering is usually counterproductive. What matters more is where the session happens. A dining table or a study corner with the door open works better than a bedroom for the student, the tutor and you, and it removes a question nobody wants to raise later. Set the place and the protocol in week one, keep the tutor's name and number on record, and check in with the student rather than supervising the tutor.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all IB and IGCSE subjects, or do we need several?
faqs.answer: One tutor can honestly cover a cluster, not a curriculum. A single tutor can hold MYP Sciences, IGCSE Chemistry and IGCSE Biology, or IGCSE Mathematics together with Additional Mathematics, at a real standard. Nobody holds Higher Level Mathematics and Higher Level English A Literature equally well, and a tutor who claims both is telling you something useful about themselves. Where a student needs two genuinely different specialisms, we propose two tutors on different evenings. In this township that is easier than elsewhere, because both can be local and both slots can sit in the late afternoon rather than being pushed to 8pm by travel.

faqs.question: Is it harder to find a tutor in Kandivali East than in Bandra or Juhu?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects, no, and for scarce ones it is less hard than the map suggests. Bandra and Juhu have more tutors living nearby, which is a genuine advantage. But Kandivali East has something they do not: a planned township dense enough that a specialist can teach three families in one evening without moving more than a few hundred metres. That economics is what brings a Diploma Programme Economics or Computer Science tutor north at all. Parents searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kandivali East are usually better served by a strong local tutor who will still be here in December than by a marginally stronger one from Khar who will not.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us in that week and we re-match at no extra cost. Three sessions is a reasonable point to know whether the student talks to this person, and personality fit is not a thing we can fully predict from a profile. We ask for one specific reason, because it makes the replacement better: too fast, too slow, no written plan, only checking homework, the student has gone quiet. The new tutor gets the diagnostic note and the work already covered, so you are not restarting from zero. Changing tutors twice in a term is rare and usually means the brief itself needs rewriting, which we will say.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for a Higher Level Diploma Programme subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for scarce Higher Level subjects it is often the only real option. HL Economics, HL Computer Science, HL Further Mathematics and some Group 1 and Group 2 languages have very few genuinely strong teachers in Mumbai, and none of them may be in the Western Suburbs. Online with a shared screen, annotated past papers and a recording the student can revisit works well for an older student who can already sit down unsupervised. It works badly for a Grade 7 student who needs an adult in the room. Most families here run one home session for teaching and one online session for review.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: Raise it immediately, because a month of nothing is information, not bad luck. We ask three questions. Is the student doing anything between sessions, or is the tutor the only study happening? Is the tutor teaching the right thing, meaning the diagnosed gap rather than the next chapter? And is the problem academic at all, because sleep, screen use and a genuine dislike of a subject all look like weak marks from outside. Depending on the answers we change the plan, change the tutor, or tell you that tuition is not the lever here. The third answer is the one platforms avoid giving and it is sometimes the correct one.

faqs.question: What happens when a session is missed because of the monsoon or exams?
faqs.answer: It gets rescheduled or converted, and you agree which in advance. In June to September the service roads off the Western Express Highway can flood, and a tutor who is already set up to teach online simply moves that week's session to a screen rather than cancelling. During examination weeks families often pause the regular slot entirely and switch to short, frequent sessions. The rule we ask both sides to keep is twenty-four hours notice where the reason is foreseeable, and the same flexibility back from the tutor. Agreeing this in the first week prevents the slow drift where two missed sessions become a month off.

faqs.question: Can the tutor come from Malad East or Borivali East instead?
faqs.answer: Yes, and those are the two easiest neighbouring matches, because Malad East and Borivali East sit on the same side of the Western Express Highway as Kandivali East. A tutor moves between them along the service road without crossing the highway or waiting at a flyover signal. Kandivali West is geographically closer but functionally further, because it means a crossing, so for a Kandivali West tutor we push the slot earlier in the afternoon. Tutors arriving by train come to Kandivali station on the Western Line and finish by rickshaw. Matching along the Western Line rather than across the highway is the rule that keeps a slot alive past October.

faqs.question: Are your tutors connected to Thakur International School or Ryan Global School?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with Thakur International School, Ryan Global School or any other school in Kandivali East or anywhere else in Mumbai. We name schools only as local context, because their calendars set the deadline rhythm families here live by and because a tutor should know which examination board a school enters students through. Some of our tutors have taught students from these schools, which is useful experience and nothing more than that. If any tutor implies an official relationship with a school, that is a reason to tell us, and we will deal with it.

sections.heading: IGCSE Years 9 to 11 and the IB Diploma Programme: two timetables in one Mumbai suburb
paragraphs: Kandivali West families are usually inside one of four structures: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through its five years, an International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) course in Years 9 to 11, or the IB Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years. What a child needs from tuition is set by which of those four they sit in, far more than by age or school.

The MYP to IGCSE step is the one families here misjudge most often. MYP reports marks against criteria, with no exam papers and no tiers, so a child can look comfortable for years. IGCSE then introduces separate papers with separate demands, and a Core or Extended decision taken subject by subject rather than for the whole child. A student can sit Extended Mathematics and Core in a second language in the same session, and the school decides on evidence.

The DP step is steeper again. Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the DP core: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Nothing in Year 11 prepares a student for carrying three HL syllabuses and a 4,000-word essay at the same time, which is exactly why the late enquiries in this suburb sound so urgent.

Our coverage runs the full span, Years 1 to 12, but the tutoring looks nothing alike at either end. A PYP or MYP student is being taught habits: reading the question, showing working, keeping a notebook that someone else could revise from. A DP2 student is being taught triage: which paper, which criterion, which deadline, this fortnight.

sections.heading: Every subject carries its own assessment, and that is where marks leak
paragraphs: On both boards the final grade is never one exam. An IGCSE subject is split across papers that test different things, and almost every DP subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA) marked by the school and moderated by the IB. Tuition that only revises content, and never touches the skills paper or the IA, leaves marks on the table in subjects where the child already knows the material.

The shape differs by subject group, which is why subject choice matters before tutor choice. Sciences carry a practical or alternative-to-practical paper that rewards apparatus, variables and tables rather than recall, and Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 candidates are often strong on theory and untrained on that paper. Languages are decided partly by speaking and coursework components marked long before the final series. Humanities turn on data response and source handling. Mathematics splits across calculator and non-calculator demands.

A worked example from this suburb. A Year 10 student at a Kandivali West address was scoring well on Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 Paper 1 and losing the four and six mark questions on Paper 2, the data response. Her answers described the figures in the extract and stopped. The fix was mechanical: a labelled diagram first, then a causal chain of two sentences linking the diagram to the data in the extract, then one evaluative sentence naming what the data cannot show. One data-response question a week, marked against the published mark scheme, in her own handwriting under time.

The same logic applies to the HL and SL decision and to Core versus Extended. A tutor does not make those calls, the school does, but a tutor supplies the evidence the school wants: marks on a full Extended paper done under timed conditions, not an impression from homework. Ask for that evidence before a tier conversation at a parent meeting, not after.

sections.heading: Kandivali East, Borivali West and Malad West: how far should a Kandivali West home tutor travel?
paragraphs: A tutor for Kandivali West should live between Malad West and Borivali West, on either side of the Western Line. That band, Malad West, Kandivali West, Kandivali East and Borivali West, is where a weekday evening slot survives a full term in Mumbai, Maharashtra. Outside it, the slot survives until the first bad evening and then starts moving around the calendar.

Kandivali West itself runs from the station westwards to the Link Road, with Mahavir Nagar and the Charkop sectors sitting towards that end and Poisar behind. Kandivali station is the pivot: it is quick to reach from anywhere in the band and slow to cross at the evening peak, so a tutor living in Kandivali East and teaching in Charkop is fighting the same bridge every week. The honest version is that east-west inside Kandivali is harder than north-south between Malad West and Borivali West.

That is the travel logic of the whole Western Suburbs. The suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so a tutor moving between Bandra and Andheri is quick off-peak and stuck at 6pm. Matching along the line, Khar to Santacruz, Malad to Kandivali, works far better than matching across it. Parents searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Kandivali West are, without knowing it, searching for exactly this: someone already inside the band.

Practically, it changes what you should ask for. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West who takes the first slot of the evening arrives on time all year. The third slot of an evening absorbs every delay ahead of it. If your child's subject is scarce and the only tutor for it lives south of Goregaon, take a weekend slot or run that subject online rather than booking a weekday evening that will quietly become a 7.45pm start by August.

sections.heading: The school calendar Kandivali West families plan around
paragraphs: Families here mostly use Ryan Global School's Kandivali campus, Thakur International School in Kandivali East and Witty International School in Malad, with JBCN International School, Borivali in reach up the line. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Ryan Global School, Thakur International School, Witty International School or any other school named on this page. They appear because their calendars set the dates tuition has to work around.

The Mumbai school year starts in June. Unit tests land in July and August, the long Diwali break falls in late October or November depending on the date, mocks run through January and February, and the Cambridge May and June series and the IB May examinations close the year, with results in August. Every pressure point a Kandivali West parent will feel sits on that skeleton, and none of it moves because a family started tuition late.

The pressure points are specific. Year 10 coursework and controlled components are usually due before the Diwali break, not in the new year, which catches families who assume December is the deadline. DP1 internal examinations fall in November and December, and they are the first honest read a DP1 student gets on whether three Higher Level subjects were the right choice. DP2 stacks IA final deadlines, the TOK essay and the Extended Essay through December, January and February, in the same weeks as mocks.

So the first session with any new tutor should include the school's own calendar on the table. A tutor who has taught students from these campuses knows when reports are issued and when the school stops accepting draft work, and that knowledge is worth more than a generic revision plan. No tutor and no platform can guarantee grades; what a calendar buys you is the chance to do the work before it is an emergency.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in Kandivali West: what holds for a full term?
paragraphs: Home tuition first, and for most families here it stays first. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West sits at your dining table, sees the actual notebook rather than a photograph of it, watches the working appear in real time, and sees the phone face down. For Years 9 to 11, where the problem is usually habits rather than intellect, nothing substitutes for that.

The honest trade-offs of home classes: the pool is limited to tutors who live inside the band, travel is priced into the hour whether anyone says so or not, a washed-out evening is a lost session rather than a shifted one, and the room matters more than parents expect. A tutor working at the end of a sofa with a television on is being paid to do a worse job than the same tutor at a table with a door that shuts.

Online widens the pool to anywhere, which is the entire argument for it. An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kandivali West is often the only realistic option for scarce choices: HL Economics, Further Mathematics, an ab initio language, Psychology, Global Politics. The trade-offs are real. Online suits a self-starting DP student and punishes a drifting Year 9. It also needs the setup to be right: a second device or a document camera pointed at the page, because a tutor who cannot see the working cannot teach the method.

Hybrid is what most of the late DP enquiries here end up on, and it works. One weekly session of IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kandivali West for the teaching, plus a short online check in the two days before an IA draft or a mock. We end up covering all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Kandivali West for the common ones and online for the rare ones, in the same family, without anyone pretending that is a compromise.

sections.heading: How is a tutor checked, and what should you check yourself?
paragraphs: Before any introduction in Kandivali West, IB Gram checks government photo identity, qualification documents, and board experience against the specific syllabus the child is sitting, then has a subject conversation with the tutor rather than a reading of their resume. Where a tutor claims school teaching, we ask which campus and which years. That is what is verified, stated plainly, and it is not the same as a police clearance.

What a platform cannot check is the part that decides whether this works: whether your child will talk to this particular adult, and whether the tutor is current on the syllabus revision in force for your child's session rather than the one they learned on. Both are findable in one trial session if you know what to ask. That is why we tell parents to run their own checks rather than treating a verified badge as the end of the matter.

Ask four things in the first call. Which syllabus code and which paper or criterion will you target first. Show me a past-paper answer you have marked, with your comments on it. What will the first session produce in writing. How will you tell me when my child has not done the work. A tutor who answers all four without flinching is usually the right choice, and a tutor who answers in adjectives is not.

The same checks apply if you find an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Kandivali West through a neighbour or a building group, which plenty of families here sensibly do. See photo identity, confirm which board they taught this academic year, and agree in advance what happens if a session is missed. If you book IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kandivali West through us, also tell us your society's visitor rule before the slot is fixed, because the gate is where first sessions get wasted.

sections.heading: Why an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West works two different years in one
paragraphs: The enquiry calendar in this pocket is not flat, and that is the one thing genuinely true here. Kandivali West is the Link Road end, with Ryan Global School's Kandivali campus close by, so the first term brings a wave of IGCSE Year 9 and Year 10 requests, while Diploma Programme requests arrive months later, in November, December and January. A tutor working this suburb effectively runs two different years inside one calendar.

Wave one runs June to October and sounds calm. A Year 9 family new to Cambridge International Education, unsure whether Extended is realistic in two subjects. A Year 10 family looking at coursework due before Diwali. The work is unglamorous: command words, timed writing, a notebook that can be revised from, one past-paper question a week per subject. There is a long runway, nothing is on fire, and the right frequency is often twice a week in one subject rather than once a week in three.

Wave two runs November to February and sounds nothing like it. The callers are families who moved board after IGCSE results in August and are now in DP1 discovering that Higher Level is not Year 11 with more pages; DP2 families with IA finals, the TOK essay and the Extended Essay converging; occasionally a Year 11 family who has just seen mock marks. The work is triage. Pick the two subjects where marks actually move, work backwards from the school's deadline rather than the examination date, and deliberately leave one subject alone.

The consequence for you is a timing decision, and it cuts both ways. If you are an IGCSE family, the good evening slots inside the Malad to Borivali band are taken by late July, so calling in September means a later slot, a weekend slot, or online. If you are a DP family, the opposite is true: DP specialists have real capacity in the first term and almost none by December. A DP1 student who books a fortnightly check in July keeps a slot that a January caller simply cannot buy.

It also changes who you should accept. In the late wave there is pressure to take whoever is free, which in this suburb usually means an IGCSE tutor being asked to teach a Higher Level course. Sometimes that is fine for a term. Often it is how a DP2 student arrives at an IA deadline with a tutor who has never seen the criteria. Say no to that match and take a hybrid arrangement instead; the right specialist online beats the wrong specialist at your table.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a grade to have moved, and a tutor who reports that it has is usually reporting a kind homework mark. What you should see is a sharper diagnosis than you had: the tutor can name the two weakest skills with marked evidence, your child can say what a question is asking before answering it, and the set work is being attempted rather than copied the morning it is due.

At one term the measures get concrete. An Internal Assessment draft went in on time without a crisis weekend. Coursework was finished before the Diwali break rather than during it. Mock marks moved on the specific paper that was targeted, even if the overall grade has not caught up yet. If none of those three things happened in a term, the problem is the match, the frequency or the subject choice, and it should be said out loud rather than paid for again.

At one exam cycle, here is the honest position: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody in Mumbai who does is selling something other than teaching. Attendance, the school's own moderation, the other five subjects, a monsoon illness in January and the child's willingness to work all sit outside what a weekly session controls. Parents often ask who the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kandivali West is. There is no single answer; there is only the best available match for one board, one year group and one evening slot.

When it is not working, say so in week three rather than at Diwali. We ask for two specifics, which session went badly and what the tutor was asked to fix, then re-shortlist from the same band. Changing tutors mid-term costs about two sessions of continuity, which is worth paying in November and rarely worth paying in February.
bullets: Four weeks: a sharper diagnosis and attempted homework, not a new grade

sections.heading: Starting home tuition in Kandivali West: what to have ready
paragraphs: Have five things to hand and the first call takes minutes rather than days. The board and year group. The subject list with syllabus codes as printed on the school's paperwork. The last report card. The term's assessment calendar. Two or three evening slots that work every week, not only this week. Saying you want a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is too broad to act on; naming two subjects and a year group is not.

The first session is a diagnosis, and you should expect it to look slightly unsatisfying. A past-paper question done under time in your child's handwriting. A short conversation about what the school has already flagged. Then a written note naming the first paper or criterion to be targeted and what will be set between sessions. No syllabus-wide plan, because a plan written before anything has been marked is decoration.

After that it is a standing weekly slot at the same time, with the room agreed in advance: a table, a plug, and a door. Two subjects in one session is the practical limit and one is usually better. If your society logs visitors, send the rule with your enquiry so the tutor is cleared before the first evening instead of calling you from the gate.

One last timing note specific to this suburb. If your child is in IGCSE Years 9 to 11, start IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kandivali West in the first term when slots exist. If your child is in DP1, book something small now rather than something urgent in December. The two-wave calendar here is predictable, which means it can be used instead of survived.

faqs.question: How much does an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kandivali West cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one before hearing the subject is guessing. What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Kandivali West depend on is the board and level, a Higher Level DP subject sitting above an MYP one; how scarce the subject is, since HL Economics or an ab initio language is far harder to staff than Year 9 Mathematics; the travel the tutor absorbs to reach your building; the session length; and whether you book one subject or two. A tutor crossing from Andheri prices that journey into the hour. One living in Charkop or Mahavir Nagar does not. Ask what the rate includes: marking, past papers, and a written note.

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually reach Charkop or Mahavir Nagar for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor already lives inside the band. Charkop and Mahavir Nagar are reachable on time from Kandivali West, Kandivali East, Borivali West and Malad West, because none of those journeys involve crossing Mumbai at the evening peak. The Link Road and S.V. Road both thicken between 6pm and 7.30pm, so a tutor based in the band treats a 7pm start as routine while a tutor coming up from Santacruz treats it as a gamble they will lose by August. If the only person who teaches your child's subject lives further south, take a weekend slot or run that subject online rather than accepting weekly lateness as normal.

faqs.question: Does my society need to issue a gate pass for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Most buildings here do, and sorting it before the first session saves a wasted evening. Many Kandivali West societies log visitors through an app or a register, and some will issue standing entry for a weekly service provider once a resident approves it. Tell us the rule while we are shortlisting, because a tutor who has to phone you from the gate every week eventually loses part of each session to it. If your society needs identity details in advance, we provide the tutor's verified photo identity. If it requires a resident to approve each entry in person, choose a slot when an adult is reliably at home.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and Higher Level has gone wrong in November. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: No, November is exactly when most Diploma Programme enquiries in Kandivali West arrive, and the work is triage rather than catch-up. A DP1 student who has just seen internal examination marks usually has one HL subject that is genuinely broken and one that looks bad because the first two were eating the week. Fix the broken one, stabilise the second, and deliberately leave the third alone for a term. Expect fewer slots than a first-term caller would have had, and expect the honest answer to involve a weekend session, a hybrid arrangement, or an online specialist rather than whoever is free locally on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: We are moving from a state board into IGCSE Year 9. When should we start home tuition?
faqs.answer: June or July, before the first unit tests, and the reason is specific to this suburb. The first-term wave here is almost entirely this: Year 9 families new to Cambridge International Education whose children are strong on content and untrained on the command words, describe, explain, compare, evaluate, that decide the marks. Starting in June gives a full term of low-pressure skill building before anything counts towards a report. Starting in September means competing for the same evening slots as every other family who waited, and doing identical work with coursework deadlines already visible before the Diwali break.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IGCSE, or only for older students?
faqs.answer: It works, with two conditions, and it is not a second-best option for every family in Mumbai. The first condition is setup: the tutor has to see the page, which means a second device or a document camera aimed at the notebook, not a webcam aimed at a face. The second is temperament. A self-starting DP student works well online and a drifting Year 9 does not, whatever the tutor's quality. For IGCSE we would normally lead with home classes and use online for a scarce subject or for a short check before a deadline rather than as the whole arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week three and we re-shortlist from the same band, at no penalty to you. We ask for two specifics rather than a general impression: which session went badly, and what the tutor was asked to fix that did not get fixed. Sometimes the answer is a different tutor. Fairly often it is the same tutor with a changed brief, because the original request was for three subjects when the child needed two, or for revision when the child needed writing practice. Changing tutors costs roughly two sessions of continuity, which is worth paying early in the year and expensive in February.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the evidence, not for reassurance. After four weeks a tutor should be able to show marked work, name the two weakest skills, and show the set work either done or not done. If the marked work exists and the school marks have not moved, that is normal and you continue. If no marked work exists, the sessions have been conversations, and that is the problem to fix. If the set work is consistently not done, no change of tutor will help until the home routine does, which is an uncomfortable conversation we would rather have at four weeks than in January.

faqs.question: Do you also cover Kandivali East, Borivali West and Malad West?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are matched as one band rather than four separate areas. A tutor living in Malad West or Borivali West is a sensible match for a Kandivali West address because the journey runs along the Western Line rather than across the Western Suburbs. The exception worth knowing is east to west inside Kandivali itself: crossing at the station in the evening peak is slower than coming down the line from Borivali West. So a Kandivali East tutor is a genuine option for a Charkop address, but take their first evening slot rather than their last.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: For the first session yes, for later sessions not necessarily, and the reason is practical rather than about trust. The first session ends in a verbal handover that is worth hearing live, and your society may need a resident present to clear a new visitor. After that, many families here leave the sessions to run with an adult somewhere in the flat, which is the arrangement most children work best under. What matters more is the room: a table, a plug, a closed door, and the television off. A session at the end of a sofa in a busy living room underperforms the same tutor at a desk.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children, one in MYP and one in IGCSE Year 10?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but check the board experience separately for each child. MYP and IGCSE are assessed in completely different ways, so a tutor fluent in criteria-based MYP feedback is not automatically current on Extended tier papers. Where one tutor can honestly cover both, back-to-back sessions in your own flat are the most efficient arrangement available in Kandivali West and save a second set of travel. Where they cannot, we would rather tell you and send two people than let one tutor improvise through the board they know less well for a whole term.

faqs.question: What happens when a session is missed because of school exams or heavy Mumbai rain?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before the first session, in writing, because this will happen. The usual arrangement is that a session cancelled by the family with reasonable notice is rescheduled, a session cancelled by the tutor is always rescheduled or dropped from the month, and a washed-out monsoon evening is moved online rather than lost. School examination weeks are a planning matter, not a cancellation matter: they are on the calendar in June, so build the term around them. Families who settle this at the start almost never argue about it later, and families who leave it vague almost always do.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE: which stage your child is actually at
paragraphs: Four structures cover almost every child in Kanjurmarg on an international pathway. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs the early years through roughly Year 5. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers years one to five, ending around Year 10. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the final two years. IGCSE occupies Years 9 to 11 under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and in Mumbai it is frequently used as the two-year run-up to the Diploma Programme rather than as an endpoint.

The Middle Years Programme confuses parents more than any of the others, because it is criterion-referenced rather than mark-based. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, each rubric is rewritten by the teacher into task-specific clarifications, and a child can write fluently and still score poorly on criterion C or D for not doing the thing the strand asked. Year five adds the Personal Project, which is a project-management test wearing academic clothing, and some schools run the optional eAssessment on top. Tutoring here is largely about teaching a student to read a rubric before starting, not after being marked.

The Diploma Programme splits into Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL): three of each, across six subject groups, plus the core. Higher Level is not the same course with extra chapters; it adds depth, an extra paper in several subjects, and a markedly heavier internal assessment load. The honest version of the HL and SL conversation is about workload across all six subjects at once, which is why a family in Runwal Greens may want all IB and IGCSE subjects across IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 handled by two home tutors in Mumbai rather than six separate arrangements.

IGCSE adds its own fork: Core and Extended tiers reach different maximum grades, and the tier decision is made far earlier than most families realise. If Extended Mathematics is the plan and Year 9 is already shaky, that is a Year 9 problem, not a Year 11 one. The two switch points worth watching in this cluster are MYP year five into DP year one, and IGCSE into the Diploma Programme, because each one changes how work is assessed, not just how hard it is.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards, and the assessment each one carries
paragraphs: Subject choice is where most of the damage is done, and it is done quietly. An IGCSE student picks ten subjects because nine felt lazy, then discovers in Year 11 that two of them need coursework supervision nobody has time for. A Diploma Programme student takes Higher Level Chemistry because a cousin did, and spends year one at the bottom of a strong set. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is often the first adult in the room with no stake in the choice, which is exactly why families here use one tutor for the diagnosis before committing to a weekly subject plan.

Each subject carries its own assessed coursework, and the deadlines do not negotiate with each other. Diploma Programme sciences carry the scientific investigation; Mathematics carries the exploration; Business Management, Economics and History each carry an Internal Assessment (IA) with a different word count and a different command structure; language courses carry oral components recorded under conditions. Over the top of all of it sit the Theory of Knowledge (TOK) essay and exhibition and the Extended Essay (EE). On the Cambridge International Education side, the equivalent pressure is the choice between a coursework route and the alternative-to-practical paper, which is a decision about what kind of student you have, not about which is easier.

A worked example, because this is the level of detail that separates a tutor who knows the component from one who knows the chapter. IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Paper 6, the alternative-to-practical paper, gives a titration table with a rough titre of 24.70 cm³ followed by 23.85 cm³ and 23.90 cm³. Weak answers average all three and lose the marks. The paper wants burette readings written to two decimal places throughout, the two concordant titres within 0.10 cm³ ticked as the ones used, and the average given to the same precision, 23.88 cm³, with the rough titre excluded because the end point was overshot. That is four or five marks of pure technique, drillable in two sessions, and it is invisible to anyone revising by reading the textbook.

The same logic holds across both boards. Marks live in the command term, the required precision, and the shape the mark scheme expects, which is why a parent who wants help across all IB and IGCSE subjects from one home tutor in Kanjurmarg should ask the tutor which components they have marked rather than which topics they can explain.

sections.heading: Which parts of Kanjurmarg and Mumbai a home tutor here covers
paragraphs: Kanjurmarg, in the Central Suburbs of Mumbai, Maharashtra, sits either side of the Central Line, and the line is the thing that decides who can realistically teach here. On the west, the lanes run off LBS Marg, north towards Bhandup and south towards Vikhroli, with Runwal Greens and the newer towers set back from the main road behind their own gates. On the east, the layout tips towards the Eastern Express Highway and the pipeline road, and addresses there are quicker to reach by car than on foot from the station. Up JVLR, between ten minutes and half an hour by auto depending on the hour, is Powai.

An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kanjurmarg will usually cover all four of those pockets in the same week, and the reason is geometry rather than goodwill. A tutor who finishes a session off LBS Marg can be at a Bhandup address one station north, or a Vikhroli address one station south, without ever joining a main road in the evening peak. That is why a Tuesday or Thursday standing slot here survives a full term when the same arrangement across the city quietly collapses by the third week of heavy traffic.

Powai is the part of this cluster that behaves differently. It is physically close, hanging off JVLR between Kanjurmarg and Andheri East, but it has no railway station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar. For a family in Kanjurmarg that is useful rather than inconvenient, because the tutor making that road leg has to pass through Kanjurmarg to make it at all. You are not competing with Powai for tutors. You are sitting at the point on the map where their journey already begins.

Two practical notes on addresses. First, tell the tutor which gate to use, not just the society name: in a multi-tower complex the difference between the LBS Marg gate and the back gate is a ten-minute walk with a bag of past papers. Second, in July and August give any JVLR leg an extra buffer, because a road leg that takes fifteen minutes in November can take three times that in a bad monsoon hour, while the Central Line into Kanjurmarg keeps moving.

sections.heading: The school calendar Kanjurmarg families actually plan around
paragraphs: Most international-board families in Kanjurmarg send their children to one of two schools: Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, which runs IGCSE and the IB Diploma Programme, or NES International School in Mulund West, which runs both IB and IGCSE pathways. A smaller number travel further west along JVLR towards the Goregaon East schools. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Hiranandani Foundation School, NES International School or any other school named on this page; those names appear here because their calendars set the dates your tutor has to work around.

Those calendars are the real timetable. The school year opens in June, and by late August the first internal assessment drafts and the first serious unit tests land together. September and October carry the Diploma Programme subject-change window, which is when a family discovers that a Higher Level choice made in May was optimistic. November and December bring mock season for IGCSE and Diploma Programme year two, and January through March is the submission crunch: internal assessments, the Extended Essay final, the Theory of Knowledge essay, and coursework deadlines stacked inside the same fortnight. April is study leave, May is the exam session, and July is when results reshape next year's plan.

The school run also sets what a weekday slot can look like. A bus coming north up LBS Marg from Mulund West, or a pickup from the Powai campus, means many children are not home, fed and ready before half past four or five. A tutor arriving at Kanjurmarg station at five is therefore well timed, and a tutor trying to start at four is usually making a promise the traffic will break. Saturday mornings are the most under-used good slot in this part of Mumbai.

Before the first session, pull three things out of the school portal: the subject guide or syllabus code for each subject, the assessment calendar for the term, and the last two marked tests with the teacher's comments. A tutor who can see the mark scheme the school used will spend session one on the actual gap instead of re-teaching a chapter the child already knows.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in Kanjurmarg?
paragraphs: Start with home tuition, because for most families here it simply works better. The child does not travel after a full school day, the textbooks and the marked papers are already on the table, and a parent in the next room hears what is happening without having to ask. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kanjurmarg has an easier commute than one going to most addresses in Mumbai, so the weekly slot tends to be real rather than aspirational, and that consistency does more for a grade than any single brilliant session.

Online earns its place in two specific situations. The first is a scarce subject: Higher Level Economics, Psychology, Computer Science, a language B option, or a Standard Level subject the school has only one teacher for. If the right specialist for that course lives in Thane or Navi Mumbai, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Kanjurmarg beats a nearby generalist every time. The second is the short, frequent session. A forty-five minute screen share annotating a past paper the night before a test is easy online and absurd in person, because the travel outweighs the teaching.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. One home session a week carries the core teaching and the accountability, and a shorter online checkpoint handles an internal assessment draft, a problem set, or the week before a mock. A Runwal Greens family running IGCSE Maths plus Diploma Programme Economics for two children often has one tutor arriving on Tuesdays and the other on screen on Saturday mornings, which is cheaper on travel and easier on the gate register.

The trade-offs, stated honestly. Home tuition is harder to reschedule: a slot cancelled on a Wednesday evening in Mumbai rarely reappears that week. The tutor's own journey bounds how early the session can start, so a 4pm request is often a no even here. Online needs a child who can sit alone with a screen and a desk, which rules out most younger learners. And a very scarce Higher Level subject may have no home option within reach at all, in which case online is not a compromise, it is the only honest answer.

sections.heading: What checking does a tutor go through before entering your flat in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Identity, qualifications and subject knowledge, in that order, and then a teaching sample. Government photo identification and an address are verified, degree and teaching documents are collected, and the subject conversation is held against a real past paper rather than a resume. References are taken where a tutor has taught in Mumbai schools or with other families. Nobody reaches a shortlist on a self-description alone.

The subject screening is the part worth understanding, because it is what separates an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kanjurmarg from a graduate with free evenings. A tutor is asked to mark a sample answer and justify the marks against the published criteria, to explain what the command term in a specific question is demanding, and to describe how they would take an internal assessment from a weak research question to a submittable draft. A tutor who talks only about concepts and never about criteria is teaching the subject, not the course.

You should run your own checks too, and they take ten minutes. Ask which syllabus version and which exam session they last taught, and listen for a specific answer. Hand them one page of your child's last marked test and ask them to mark it in front of you. Ask what the first three sessions will cover and why in that order. Confirm that the person described in the profile is the person who will arrive every week, because substitution without notice is the single most common complaint in home tuition anywhere in Mumbai.

The society side is simple but needs doing once. Register the tutor at the gate as a recurring visitor rather than a fresh guest every week, which in Runwal Greens and most Kanjurmarg towers means one entry in the register and a standing pass. Hold sessions in the living room or at the dining table with the door open, not in a bedroom. If your flat is noisy with a younger sibling, book the clubhouse study room for the slot instead and tell the tutor which block it is in.
bullets: Photo identification, address and qualification documents verified before shortlisting
Subject screening against a real past paper and its published mark scheme
Ask the tutor to mark one page of your child's last test in front of you
Confirm the person on the profile is the person who arrives each week

sections.heading: Why is it easier to book a home tutor in Kanjurmarg than in Powai?
paragraphs: Because the tutors who teach Powai arrive through Kanjurmarg. Powai has no station of its own, so a tutor living anywhere up or down the Central Line takes a local to Kanjurmarg and finishes the trip by road. Kanjurmarg is the first address on that journey where a tutor can teach, not the hardest one to reach.

The effect shows up in the schedule rather than in any brochure. A tutor who has a Powai family at seven can take a Kanjurmarg family at half past five on the way in, or at eight on the way back to the station. Neither of those slots needs a second road leg, so the tutor is not mentally pricing in forty minutes of JVLR before saying yes. That is the difference between a tutor who agrees to a slot and a tutor who agrees and is still turning up in February.

It also widens the shortlist, which matters more than speed. If a dozen tutors on this line can reach your flat without rearranging their week, you get to choose on syllabus fit: the person who has actually marked the component your child is failing, or supervised the internal assessment they are stuck on, instead of the person who happens to live closest. In most of Mumbai that choice is a luxury. Here it is the normal condition, and a parent who does not use it is wasting the one advantage the postcode gives them.

The honest limit: none of this creates extra slots in the seven to eight o'clock window that every family in Mumbai wants. That hour is contested everywhere, and the families who get it are the ones who booked a standing slot in June rather than in December. Scarce Higher Level subjects stay scarce too. A tutor who already holds three Powai evenings may only have two days that work for Kanjurmarg at all, so flexibility on the day of the week buys you far more than flexibility on the fee.
bullets: Kanjurmarg is the station end of a Powai tutor's existing commute
Earlier and later slots open up because no second road leg is needed

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle in Mumbai
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look for three things: the sessions actually happened on the agreed day, your child can say what they are bad at in specific language rather than saying the subject is hard, and homework is being attempted before the session instead of during it. Four weeks is roughly four to six hours of teaching in one subject. That is enough to map a gap and build a habit, and it is not enough to move a grade on a syllabus built over two years.

At one term the evidence should be visible on paper. Topic test scores move, usually unevenly, and the comment that changes first is not about effort but about understanding what the question wanted. Internal assessment drafts arrive before the school deadline rather than during it. A Diploma Programme year two student in Kanjurmarg who was handing in a Chemistry investigation the night before should, by term end, be bringing a draft to the session a fortnight early and asking about the evaluation criterion. If none of that has shifted in a term, the plan is wrong and changing one variable is overdue.

At one exam cycle you can read mock-to-final movement and predicted grades against outcomes, and that is the only honest measurement window for a full board course. It is also where expectations need stating plainly: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor who has read a mark scheme would. Attendance, the work done between sessions, the school's own teaching and how early help started all matter more than any single tutor. What tutoring reliably improves is preparation and technique. The grade follows from those more often than not, which is a different sentence from a promise.

When a tutor is not working out, say so early and say what is wrong: the explanations are not landing, the sessions drift, the slot keeps moving. Some of those are fixable in one conversation, because a tutor given specific feedback usually changes the structure of the next session. If it is a fit problem rather than a method problem, ask for a replacement. A new tutor gets the same brief plus everything learned from the first attempt, which is why the second match usually settles faster than the first.
bullets: Four weeks: consistent attendance, specific self-diagnosis, homework done beforehand
One term: topic tests moving and coursework drafts arriving before the deadline
One exam cycle: the only fair window to judge a full IB or IGCSE course

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Kanjurmarg: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four things make the first session useful instead of introductory. The last report card, including the comments nobody reads. The subject guide or syllabus code for each subject you want covered, because 0580 and 0607 are not the same conversation. The last two marked tests, uncorrected. And the term assessment calendar, so the tutor can see which fortnight is going to hurt before it arrives.

Then settle the logistics once, in writing, and they stop costing you anything. A fixed day and time for the term. A named gate and tower, with a standing visitor pass at the society office. A table with a lamp that is not the kitchen counter during dinner. One adult at home, not supervising, just present. And an agreed rule for a missed session: whether it is made up on a Saturday, moved online, or dropped.

The first session is a diagnostic, and a good tutor will spend most of it finding out where the student actually is rather than teaching from page one. Expect past paper questions used as probes, some reading aloud of the child's own answers, and a short plan at the end naming the first two things to fix. If you get a plan that could have been written without meeting your child, that is a signal, and it is better to act on it in week one than in week six.

Parents searching for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Kanjurmarg usually mean something narrower than the phrase suggests: the tutor who knows the component, turns up every week, and tells you the truth at four weeks. That is a findable thing here, more easily than in most of Mumbai, because the Central Line brings the right people to Kanjurmarg station anyway. Send the board, the year, the subjects and two slots, and the shortlist comes back built around what your child is actually failing.
bullets: Have the last report card, syllabus codes and two marked tests ready
Fix one day and time for the term rather than rescheduling weekly

faqs.question: How much does an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kanjurmarg cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one before hearing the subject is guessing. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Kanjurmarg move with five things: the board and level, since Higher Level and Extended work costs more than Middle Years Programme support; how scarce the subject is, because a Higher Level Economics or Psychology specialist is rarer than a Maths tutor; the session length and how many sessions a week; the tutor's own experience with that specific component; and travel, which is lighter here than in Powai because the tutor is already coming down the Central Line. Ask for the per-session figure and the term commitment together, since a lower rate with a tutor who cancels is the expensive option.

faqs.question: Will a tutor really travel to Kanjurmarg for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more readily than to many Mumbai addresses. The tutors who teach Powai families already take a local to Kanjurmarg and finish the journey by road, so a Kanjurmarg session is either the first stop of their evening or the last one on the way back to the station. That removes the extra road leg they would otherwise be weighing up. Flexibility on the day of the week helps more than anything else: a tutor holding Powai evenings on Monday and Wednesday can usually offer Tuesday, Thursday or Saturday here without rearranging anything.

faqs.question: How does gate access and a visitor pass work at Runwal Greens or a similar society?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a recurring visitor rather than logging a new guest every week. In Runwal Greens and most Kanjurmarg towers that means the flat owner informs the society office or the app, the tutor's name and identification are recorded, and the gate issues a standing pass for the agreed day and time. Tell the tutor which gate to use and the tower number, because the walk between gates in a large complex is longer than it looks. If your society requires a fresh approval each visit, approve it in advance for the term so nobody is stuck at the gate at six o'clock.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one subject for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Within a board, adjacent subjects often sit with one person: Mathematics and Physics, Chemistry and Biology at IGCSE level, Economics and Business Management at Standard Level. Across Higher Level sciences it is less common and you should be suspicious of a tutor who claims three of them. The practical benefit of combining is scheduling: one tutor, one slot, one gate pass, and one person who can see that the Physics internal assessment and the Maths exploration are due the same fortnight. The risk is depth, so test each subject separately in the first session.

faqs.question: Does online tuition actually work for IB internal assessments?
faqs.answer: For internal assessment drafting it often works better than in person. The work is a document, so a shared screen with live comments beats two people leaning over a laptop, and the session can be thirty minutes at the point the student is stuck rather than a fixed hour on Thursday. Where online is weaker is the lab and data side of a sciences investigation, and anything needing diagram work under pressure. The common pattern among families here is the home session for teaching and a short online checkpoint for drafts, which is why hybrid ends up being the default rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three or four sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us what is wrong specifically and ask for a change. Vague dissatisfaction is hard to act on; a sentence like the explanations are too fast, or the sessions have no structure, or two slots have already moved, is actionable. Some of that is fixable with one conversation, because tutors given concrete feedback restructure the session. If it is a fit problem, a replacement is arranged and the new tutor gets the original brief plus what the first attempt revealed, so the second match usually settles faster. Raise it at week two or three, not at the end of term.

faqs.question: My child is in Diploma Programme year one at Hiranandani Foundation School and wants to move Higher Level Chemistry to Standard Level. Can a tutor help decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a decision worth a session on its own before the school window closes. A tutor who has taught both levels can look at the actual marked work and separate two different problems: the content is too hard, or the workload across all six subjects is too heavy. Those have opposite answers. The school controls the deadline and the paperwork, so check the subject-change window with the Diploma coordinator first. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with the school, so the advice you get is about your child's evidence rather than about anyone's timetable.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Ask a narrower question first, because one month is four to six teaching hours and marks rarely move that fast. Check whether the sessions happened on time, whether homework is being done before the session, and whether your child can now name the specific thing they get wrong. If all three are yes, the method is working and the marks lag. If any is no, change one variable now: the slot, the structure, or the tutor. Waiting until the term ends to find out is the expensive version of this decision, and nobody can guarantee a grade recovery either way.

faqs.question: Do you cover Powai, Bhandup and Vikhroli with the same tutors who come to Kanjurmarg?
faqs.answer: Largely yes, because they are all on or just off the same line. Bhandup is one station north and Vikhroli one station south of Kanjurmarg on the Central Line, so a tutor teaching in one can teach in the others on different evenings without touching the Eastern Express Highway at peak hour. Powai is reached by road up JVLR instead, which adds time but is the journey these tutors are already making. If you are coordinating two children at two addresses in this cluster, say so at the start, since it changes which tutors can take both.

faqs.question: What happens to a home tuition session missed because of heavy rain or a train disruption?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule before it happens, in the first week. The three workable options are a Saturday make-up, a switch to online for that session only, or treating it as dropped with no charge, and different tutors prefer different ones. In July and August in Mumbai this will come up, so the sensible default is to move the session online the same evening rather than lose the week, since the student is already at home with the books out. Kanjurmarg fares better than most here because the Central Line usually keeps running when JVLR and the highway do not.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the home classes?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, but not in the room. Presence matters for safety and it keeps the session honest in both directions; sitting in the session usually makes a teenager quieter and less willing to admit confusion. Set the table up in the living or dining area with the door open, and stay within earshot. If both parents work late, a grandparent or any responsible adult at home is fine, and the tutor should know who will open the door. Tell the tutor in advance if nobody will be there, because many will reschedule rather than teach alone with a child.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE Core and Extended taught differently by the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a tutor who treats them as the same course with fewer questions is the wrong tutor. The tiers share content but differ in the papers sat, the grade ceiling available, and the kind of question asked: Extended papers push further into multi-step and unfamiliar applications. A good tutor will tell you honestly whether the Extended tier is realistic from where your child currently is, and in which term the decision has to be made. If the answer is that Extended is a stretch, that is useful information in Year 9 and useless in Year 11.

sections.heading: How IB Gram finds an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Kasarvadavali
paragraphs: A request from Kasarvadavali is handled as a west Thane request from the first minute. The useful question is not who the strongest Chemistry teacher in Mumbai happens to be. It is who can ring your doorbell at 6.45pm on a Tuesday in July and still be ringing it in November. Those are two different lists, and we start from the second one, then look for subject depth inside it. A tutor who cannot hold the slot teaches nobody, however good the subject history reads on a profile.

That is why the first thing we ask for is your cross road, not just a pin code. Kasarvadavali runs along Ghodbunder Road near the depot and the Ovala side, and a tutor who lives off the same stretch has a ten minute ride to your gate. A tutor living near Thane station has a journey that roughly doubles between April and August. We take the slot you want, the board, the year group and the subjects, then filter the pool by where the tutor actually sleeps at night before we filter by anything else.

The shortlist that comes back is short on purpose. You get two or three profiles, each stating the boards taught, the year groups handled, the subject history and, in plain words, the area the tutor lives in and the route they will take. You speak to them yourself before anything is booked, and travel belongs in that first conversation rather than after it. If a tutor says honestly that your timing is difficult for her, that is useful, and we would far rather you hear it in week zero than in week five.

The first session then runs at the real time you intend to keep, not at a convenient Sunday noon. A session at 7pm on a working weekday tells you more about whether this arrangement survives the monsoon than any weekend trial ever will. Once that session has happened at the honest hour, the standing weekly slot is confirmed and the tutor starts planning around your school's own assessment dates.
bullets: 1. Send the board, year group, subjects, preferred slot and your Ghodbunder Road cross street.
2. We filter to tutors living between Manpada and the Kasarvadavali end, then by subject.
3. You get two or three profiles that state where each tutor lives and travels from.
4. You speak to the shortlist yourself and ask about the weekday evening commute.

sections.heading: Which programmes and year groups Kasarvadavali families need covered
paragraphs: Homes on this stretch do not all follow one programme. In a single building you will find a Year 4 child in the Primary Years Programme (PYP), a Year 9 starting Cambridge IGCSE with Cambridge International Education, and a Diploma Programme (DP) student in her second year counting down to the May series. Primary, Middle Years Programme (MYP) and IGCSE requests from Kasarvadavali arrive in broadly similar numbers, with DP smaller but far more intense per student. Any tutor pool serving this area has to cover all of it, because the second child in a house is rarely on the same track as the first.

In PYP the work is reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud, and a home tutor here is often repairing confidence rather than teaching content. MYP is where parents first get genuinely confused: the subject groups, the four criteria marked out of eight in every subject, the interdisciplinary tasks and the MYP 5 ePortfolio bear no resemblance to the percentage marks an Indian board parent grew up with. We match across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 with a home tutor Mumbai families can keep for longer than a single term.

IGCSE covers Years 9 to 11 in most schools here, and it is front loaded with decisions: how many subjects, which sciences, Core or Extended tiers, and whether a coursework option or a written alternative is being offered. The Diploma Programme covers Years 11 and 12 and loads six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), on top of the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service. A tutor working with a DP student is managing a calendar as much as a syllabus.

Mid-year board switches are common on this side of Thane, usually a child moving from an ICSE or CBSE school into a Cambridge or IB stream. The content gap is smaller than parents fear and the method gap is larger: command words, showing working that earns method marks, and writing to a published mark scheme instead of to a teacher's preference. That transition is a definable piece of work with an end date, and it is worth being explicit about it when you first describe your child.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL/SL and Core/Extended: what a Kasarvadavali shortlist has to cover
paragraphs: The decision that costs families here the most is not which tutor to hire, it is which subjects at which tier. At IGCSE, Core and Extended are separate papers with separate ceilings: Extended Mathematics 0580 sits on Papers 2 and 4 and keeps the whole grade range open, while Core sits on Papers 1 and 3 and caps it. A Year 9 student placed in Core after one weak Year 8 term then needs someone to build the evidence for moving back up, and that argument has to be made before the school's option deadline closes, not after the mocks.

In the Diploma Programme the same question appears as Higher Level against Standard Level. The HL extras are concrete rather than vague: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL carries a third written paper, Economics HL adds a policy paper that rewards quantitative handling, the sciences keep the same Internal Assessment (IA) but carry a heavier paper load, and Language A HL adds a further written task. Choosing three HL subjects is choosing where your child spends her evenings for two years, so it deserves a conversation with someone who has taught both tiers.

Every subject also carries internal work with its own internal deadline, and those deadlines are what actually crowd a term. The DP sciences each need a scientific investigation, Mathematics needs an exploration, Business Management needs a research project, Language A carries written and oral components, and Visual Arts runs an exhibition with a curatorial rationale. At IGCSE the equivalent pressure lands as the practical paper or the alternative-to-practical, plus whichever coursework option the school has chosen. Nobody sits only written papers any more, and a tutor who only drills written papers is only doing half the job.

Parents here often ask for all IB and IGCSE subjects with one home tutor in Kasarvadavali, and until roughly MYP 3 that is realistic. From IGCSE onwards it stops being realistic: the person who can take Extended Chemistry 0620 to the top band is rarely the person who can teach a Language B oral well. The usual honest answer is one tutor for the sciences and mathematics, one for languages and humanities, and a willingness to add a third only for a subject that is genuinely scarce.
bullets: IGCSE Core against Extended: different papers, different ceilings, one school deadline.
HL against SL: extra papers and heavier reading, with the same Internal Assessment.

sections.heading: Which parts of Thane and Mumbai a Kasarvadavali home tutor covers
paragraphs: A tutor who takes a weekly Kasarvadavali slot generally also teaches in Manpada and along the Ghodbunder Road length between the two, and sometimes in Balkum on the station side. That is the honest radius, and it is narrower than a map suggests. Thane belongs to greater Mumbai, Maharashtra, but inside Thane the distances behave like a line rather than a grid: west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada, with Kasarvadavali sitting at the far western end of that line.

The arithmetic families already know: a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and takes nearly an hour in the evening. The Central Line from Thane to Kalyan and the Trans-Harbour Line to Vashi are irrelevant to that last leg, because the last leg is road. Thane tutors cover Thane, and Mulund tutors sometimes cross over, which matters because NES International School sits in Mulund West and some tutors already make that trip for school-adjacent work.

This shapes who can realistically keep a weekday slot with you. A tutor based nearby will stack two students back to back, one in Manpada at 5.30pm and one in Kasarvadavali at 7pm, and the arrangement is stable because neither trip crosses the full Ghodbunder crawl. A tutor coming from the station side has to treat your session as the only thing she does that evening, which makes it expensive in her own time and the first thing she drops when something else appears. Supply here is local supply.

The Thane and Mumbai pools are not interchangeable either. Pulling a Western Suburbs tutor across for a weekday evening lesson in Kasarvadavali does not survive a term under present road conditions, however willing everyone is in the first week. Weekend sessions from further out can work, and online sessions from anywhere in Mumbai work for the right kind of task, but the weekday home visit needs a tutor who lives on this side of the Ghodbunder stretch.
bullets: Core radius: Kasarvadavali, Manpada and the Ghodbunder Road length between them.
Balkum is reachable but sits on the station side of the evening traffic.

sections.heading: Which schools do Kasarvadavali families use, and when does their calendar bite?
paragraphs: Families on this stretch mostly use Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, which runs a Cambridge IGCSE pathway, and NES International School in Mulund West, which covers both IB and IGCSE. Billabong High International School also has a Thane campus that some households here choose. The practical consequence of a Mulund West school for a Kasarvadavali address is bus time: a child on that route leaves early and gets home late, so a tutor arriving before about 5.30pm is arriving to an empty flat or an exhausted child.

The Mumbai school year sets the pressure points, and they are predictable enough to plan against. June and July are the quiet months when a new tutor should be starting. August and September bring the first graded MYP tasks and IGCSE class tests, which is when parents realise a subject has gone wrong. October and November are the worst compression in the year: school mocks, DP Internal Assessment drafts and the Extended Essay first full version land together. January and February are final mocks and the last internal deadlines, and from late February the IGCSE and DP written papers begin.

What the school sets and what the board sets are different things, and this confuses parents every year. The board publishes the syllabus, the mark schemes and the final examination series. The school sets option deadlines, internal assessment submission dates, mock timetables and the order in which topics are taught. A tutor who asks for your school's own deadline sheet in the first session is doing the right thing, because teaching the syllabus in the wrong order to a Singhania or NES International School student wastes a whole term.

Naming these schools here is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School, NES International School, Billabong High International School or any other school named on this page. We do not represent them, we do not speak for their admissions, and no tutor on the platform should ever imply otherwise. What a tutor can legitimately know is how a given school paces its syllabus and when its internal deadlines usually fall.
