sections.heading: How IB and IGCSE home tutors in Marine Drive are checked, and what you should check yourself
paragraphs: Every tutor put forward for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Marine Drive request has been through the same four checks before you see the profile: identity, qualification, subject evidence and reference. Identity is a government photograph document matched to the person who actually turns up. Qualification is the certificate itself, not the claim on the form. Reference is a previous family or school, contacted. Subject evidence is the one that matters most on the Mumbai panel, and it is the narrowest.

Subject evidence is not 'teaches Physics'. It is which board, which level, which components, and what the tutor has personally prepared students for or marked. For a two-board booking that check is run twice, once per child. A tutor claiming both IGCSE Mathematics Extended and DP Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is asked in the same conversation about Paper 2 without a calculator and about the exploration criteria. A vague answer on either half disqualifies them from the pairing even when the other half is strong, because a shared block has no room for a weak hour.

What a parent should check is different, and it takes about ten minutes. Ask which specific component the tutor would start with for each child, and why that one. Ask what they want the elder child to bring to the first session. Ask what they will not teach. A tutor who answers all three concretely is worth a trial; one who answers in general language about confidence and fundamentals is not. Then watch the first two visits for the handover itself: whether the second child gets a planned session or the tail end of the first child's hour.

IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no verification process can promise that a checked tutor will suit your particular child. The checks remove the worst outcomes, a fabricated qualification or a subject bluff, and that is a real but limited thing to have done. Judgement about fit stays with the parent, which is exactly why a paid trial block exists and why replacing a tutor is treated as an ordinary administrative step rather than as a complaint that needs justifying.
bullets: Identity document matched to the person who arrives at your door.
Certificates seen, not qualifications taken on trust from a form.
Subject evidence checked per board and per component, twice for a pairing.
Ask each tutor which component they would start with for each child.
Watch whether the handover is planned or one child gets leftovers.

sections.heading: A worked two-children brief from a Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road building
paragraphs: Here is a brief of the kind that arrives from this stretch of South Mumbai most weeks, with the details changed. Two children in a sea-facing flat near Charni Road. The elder is in DP1 at Cathedral and John Connon School taking Chemistry Higher Level, and her problem is specific: her scientific investigation is a rate-of-reaction experiment with an independent variable too weak to produce a measurable range, and she is losing marks on Paper 2 extended-response questions where data is given and the conclusion has to be argued rather than recalled. The younger is in Year 10 at Bombay International School on Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 Extended, and his problem is Paper 2: he can do the algebra with a calculator and falls apart without one.

That brief is one tutor, not two, because a Chemistry Higher Level teacher who is also confident with 0580 Extended is a common enough profile. The slot is built as a two-hour block on a Tuesday evening. The first seventy-five minutes go to the elder child, because the investigation deadline is fixed and the Paper 2 skill takes weeks to build: two sessions rebuilding the experiment so the variable gives a real range, then data-based questions from past papers with the conclusion written out every time in the command-term language the examiner expects. The remaining forty-five minutes go to the younger child's non-calculator work: surds, index laws, fraction arithmetic and the estimation habit Paper 2 quietly rewards.

By January the split inverts. The elder child's IA is submitted and her TOK essay is done, while the younger child is weeks from his first full mock series, so he takes the longer half and she takes a shorter review slot on her weaker topics. In March, once she is inside the DP2 run-up, it flips back. Writing that re-balancing into the arrangement at the start, as a rule both children have heard, rather than renegotiating it under deadline pressure in front of them, is the single thing that makes a sibling booking survive a full year.

The same brief with different subjects would not work at all. If the elder were taking History Higher Level and the younger IGCSE Physics, the honest answer is two tutors on two evenings. A request for IB and IGCSE private tuition in Marine Drive that is forced into one person against the subject evidence buys a strong hour and a thin one, and the thin hour is always the younger child's. The convenience of a single visit is worth something, but it is not worth a term of the second child's subject.
bullets: Elder child: Chemistry HL investigation plus Paper 2 data-based responses.
Younger child: 0580 Extended Paper 2, the non-calculator paper.
Two-hour Tuesday block split seventy-five and forty-five minutes.
Split inverts in January, then inverts back for the DP2 run-up.

sections.heading: What does progress look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see changed working, not changed grades. The younger child showing non-calculator method on paper instead of jumping to an answer. The elder one writing a conclusion that names the trend and its limitation. Both of them arriving at the session with the right book already open. That is what a month of honest home tuition buys, and a tutor who promises a grade jump inside a month has told you something useful about themselves.

At one term, roughly three months, marks should start moving on the components that were actually worked on, and only those. A child who was losing marks on 0580 Paper 2 should be losing fewer there while Paper 4 sits roughly where it was, because that is what the sessions covered. A DP child's IA draft should be coming back from the teacher with structural comments rather than fundamental ones. If nothing in the school's own written feedback has shifted in tone by the end of a term, the arrangement needs a direct conversation, not a fourth month of patience.

Across a full exam cycle the honest picture is partial. Some children move two grades, some move one, some hold a grade they were going to lose, and a few do not move because teaching was never the binding problem. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not pretend the variables are controllable: attendance, the school's own teaching, whether the child reads the feedback, and in a two-child household whether the January split was respected or quietly re-argued every week. What a parent can reasonably hold a tutor to is attendance, preparation, accurate marking against the real criteria, and a straight answer when progress stalls.

The limits are worth stating plainly, because a sibling booking invites the opposite assumption. A visiting tutor cannot undo an unsuitable subject choice made two years earlier, cannot replace school laboratory time, and cannot make an exam-year timetable less crowded than it is. What they can do is make the available hours count, catch a misread command term before it costs a whole paper, and tell a parent early when the real answer is a level change or a subject change rather than more hours.
bullets: Four weeks: changed working and better preparation, not changed grades.
One term: movement on the components taught, not across the board.
Exam cycle: real but partial, and never promised in advance.
Hold a tutor to attendance, marking accuracy and honest stall reports.

sections.heading: Starting home classes for both children in the same week
paragraphs: Starting is deliberately short. Send one message with both children's year and board, their school, the subjects you want covered, the two evenings that genuinely work, and whatever is already going wrong. You get two or three profiles back with the pairing reasoning written out, and you pick one for a trial. For all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Marine Drive the trial is a single two-hour visit covering both children, because a pairing has to be watched before it can be judged.

Prepare four things before that visit. The last report or mark sheet for each child, including the component breakdown if the school provides one. Any marked work with the teacher's comments still on it, which is far more useful than a clean notebook. The deadline sheet for both children on one page. And a decision about where the sessions happen: the dining table, the study, or whichever room the younger child cannot see a television from. A home tutor who walks in to all four of those saves the first half hour of real teaching time.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to spend the opening twenty minutes with each child finding where the actual break is, rather than starting at the top of a chapter. Expect to be told something you did not want to hear about at least one of the two. By the end of the visit you should have a written plan: which component each child starts on, what the next four weeks cover, and what the tutor needs from the school. If that does not arrive, ask for it before the second session rather than after the first month.

Replacement is part of the arrangement rather than a failure of it. If the fit is wrong after the trial or after a month, say so and a different tutor is matched; the usual cause is pace or personality rather than knowledge, and changing is faster than enduring. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is engaged the same way wherever the address is: one message, a short shortlist with reasoning, a trial block, then a standing weekly slot that moves with the deadlines.
bullets: One message: both children's years, boards, schools, subjects and free evenings.
Trial is a single two-hour visit covering both children in sequence.
Bring the last report and marked work with teacher comments attached.
Expect a written four-week plan by the end of the first visit.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor teach both my children in the same visit in Marine Drive?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, provided their subjects are related. One home tutor covering two children in a single visit works when the subjects sit in the same family, for example Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics Extended for the younger child and IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Standard Level for the elder. The visit is booked as one block and split, commonly seventy-five minutes and forty-five, with the longer half going to whichever child has the nearer deadline. It stops working when the subjects are genuinely distant, when one child is inside an exam series, or when the age gap is wide enough that one needs criterion-based MYP teaching and the other a Diploma internal assessment. Then two tutors on two evenings is the better arrangement.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Marine Drive depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on board, level, subject scarcity, travel and session length, and on whether one tutor or two is doing the work. Diploma Higher Level costs more per hour than IGCSE Core, because fewer tutors can teach it and the preparation behind each session is heavier. A scarce subject costs more than a common one at the same level. Travel weighs less on this stretch than in the Mumbai suburbs, since tutors are matched within the island, but a two-hour sibling block is usually priced differently from two separate single hours. No price list is quoted here, because rates are set by individual tutors. Ask for the rate in writing before the trial, including what a cancelled session costs.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get into a sea-facing building on Marine Drive in the evening?
faqs.answer: Through the watchman's register in most of the older blocks on Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road, rather than through a pre-registered digital gate pass. Tell the desk the tutor's name and the standing day and time once, and after two or three visits the tutor is a known face who is waved through. Two practical points. The lifts in these buildings are small and slow at around seven in the evening, so build five minutes into the slot instead of treating a late start as lateness. And if your building keeps a photograph or identity record for regular visitors, get that done in the first week rather than at the fourth session, when it becomes an argument.

faqs.question: My children's schools have different exam weeks. Does the shared slot still work?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only if you agree in advance that the split will move. Cathedral and John Connon School and Bombay International School do not run their internal examinations in the same weeks, and the Cambridge and IB external sessions do not align either. The arrangement that works is a fixed two-hour block with a variable split: the child nearer an assessment takes the longer half that month and gives it back the next. Households that insist on an even division every week are the ones that break in January, when Diploma internal assessment deadlines, the TOK essay and IGCSE mocks all land inside the same fortnight and somebody has to lose time.

faqs.question: Is an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Marine Drive a real alternative?
faqs.answer: Yes for some cases and no for others, and the deciding factor is what the session needs to show. Online works well for a scarce Higher Level subject where the right teacher is not in South Mumbai, for the monsoon weeks when visits get cancelled anyway, and for short targeted revision in the final month before papers. It works badly for a young child, for anything with a practical component, and for a sibling handover, where the second child reliably gets a thinner session than they would in person. Most two-child households on this stretch end up hybrid: one visit a week plus a shorter online review and marking session.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is good with one child and not the other?
faqs.answer: Say so early, because this is the most common failure in a sibling booking and it is straightforward to fix. The usual pattern is that the tutor's real strength is the elder child's subject, and the younger one is getting a competent but unenthusiastic forty-five minutes at the end of a long evening. Two options follow. Keep that tutor for the child they suit and match a second tutor for the other, which costs more but fixes the actual problem. Or move the younger child entirely if their subject is better served elsewhere. A replacement does not require a complaint, a reason beyond fit, or a difficult conversation with the tutor.

faqs.question: How long does a tutor take to travel from Worli or Colaba to Marine Drive?
faqs.answer: Longer than the map suggests, because short distances here are slow. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. The Coastal Road has improved arrivals from Worli and Prabhadevi noticeably, which is why some tutors who could not hold a six o'clock booking here a few years ago now can. Tutors are still matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, because a long evening commute is what ends an arrangement by the third month, whatever everyone intended in week one.

faqs.question: There is no progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the component-level picture before changing anything. A month is long enough to see changed working and better preparation, not changed grades, so the first question is whether the tutor can show you which specific papers or criteria were worked on and what the child's output on those looks like now compared with four weeks ago. If that answer is concrete and the school's feedback is starting to shift in tone, give it a full term. If the answer is general, about confidence and basics, that is the signal to change tutor. Nobody can guarantee grades, but a tutor should always be able to name what they taught and what it changed.

faqs.question: Do you need a parent at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but for a sibling booking it helps for the first two or three visits. The handover between two children is the fragile part of the arrangement, and an adult in the next room during the first fortnight makes it settle faster, because both children learn that the split is a rule rather than a negotiation. After that, most families leave the tutor and children to the session, with an adult or household staff in the flat for the obvious reasons. What does need a parent is the end-of-month conversation: five minutes on what each child covered and what shifts next month, which is worth far more than hovering during the hour.

faqs.question: What does "best IB and IGCSE tutor in Marine Drive" actually mean when parents search it?
faqs.answer: In practice it means the right fit for your two children, which no ranking can tell you in advance. There is no single ordering of tutors on this stretch, and anyone offering one is selling something. What you can compare is specific and answerable: which board and level each tutor has actually taught, which component they would start with for each of your children, how they propose to split a shared two-hour block, and what they say they will not teach. A tutor who answers those four clearly is the useful match for your household, whatever the search phrase implies about league tables that do not exist.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor also prepare my younger child who is still in MYP?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on how far apart the two children are. A Middle Years Programme year four or five child and an IGCSE Year 10 child can often share a tutor, because the content is close and the MYP criteria map onto exam skills without much translation. An MYP year two child and a DP2 child rarely should: the younger one needs criterion-referenced tasks and a slower pace, and in a shared block they predictably get the tired end of the evening. If the gap is that wide, a separate shorter slot on a different day works better than squeezing both children into one visit to save a journey.

marine-drive.closingCta: Send one message with both children's years, boards, schools and subjects, and the two evenings that work. You get two or three tutor profiles back with the pairing reasoning written out, not just names. Pick one, run a single two-hour trial covering both children, and decide after you have watched the handover. If the fit is wrong, ask for a different tutor; that is normal here.

sections.heading: How do we find an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Matunga who can teach both boards?
paragraphs: We start from the board and the component, not the postcode. A request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Matunga gets read as two separate questions: which board and which year the student is in and which papers or internal assessments land next, and only then who can realistically reach your address on a weekday evening. Getting that order right is the difference between a tutor who knows the subject and a tutor who knows the assessment.

The sequence is short and you control most of it. 1. You send the board, the year, the subjects and two time windows that actually work in your household. 2. We shortlist tutors who have taught that exact component recently, filtered down to people who already travel the Matunga–Kings Circle stretch or live within a short run of Matunga and Matunga Road stations. 3. You see profiles with qualifications, boards and levels taught, and years of teaching, and you choose who you want to meet. 4. sections.heading: PYP, MYP, DP and IGCSE under one roof in Matunga
paragraphs: Matunga is unusual for Mumbai because one campus covers nearly the whole range. Don Bosco International School here runs both the International Baccalaureate (IB) and Cambridge IGCSE, so a family can keep a Primary Years Programme (PYP) child and an IGCSE or Middle Years Programme (MYP) sibling in the same school run. JBCN International School, Parel, a short drive down from Matunga, offers the same two pathways, and between them they account for most of the international-board demand in this part of the island.

Each stage wants a different kind of teacher. PYP asks for someone comfortable with inquiry units, transdisciplinary themes and no textbook to drill from, which is why a useful PYP tutor spends more time on reading fluency and number sense than on worksheets. MYP asks for someone who can read the four achievement-level criteria in a subject group and explain, with the student's own work on the table, why a piece sits at level 5 and not level 7. IGCSE Years 9 to 11 asks for syllabus and past-paper discipline. The Diploma Programme (DP) asks for subject depth plus the Internal Assessment (IA), Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK) load stacked on top of six subjects.

The handover from Year 11 into DP1 is the hardest thing to tutor here, and Matunga sees a lot of it precisely because so many students stay in the same school across both boards. Cambridge International Education rewards complete, well-structured answers against a published mark scheme. The IB rewards argument, method, reflection and honest evaluation against criteria descriptors. A student who was strong at IGCSE can spend a whole first term of DP1 writing excellent IGCSE answers and scoring poorly for it. A tutor who has taught both, which tutors working this pocket often have, corrects that habit in weeks instead of terms.

sections.heading: Subject choice across both boards: HL, SL, Core and Extended
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision that changes how much tutoring a student will need two years later. At IGCSE the tiering call comes first. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is entered at Core or Extended, and only Extended covers the algebra, functions and trigonometry that Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level (HL) later assumes a student already owns. A Core entry is also capped at the top end. The decision quietly closes a door long before anyone in the family notices it has closed.

Here is a worked example from the component itself. An Extended candidate at 0580 sits a short-answer paper without a calculator and a longer structured paper with one. The same topic, compound percentage change, turns up in both, but the short paper wants one clean line of method and the long paper awards method marks for setting out the multiplier before any arithmetic happens. A student who has only ever practised with a calculator drops marks on the first paper and then drops method marks on the second by writing the answer with no working above it. A home tutor handling this properly spends one session on written method, one on non-calculator fluency, and then sets a mixed timed set, rather than re-teaching percentages from scratch.

At Diploma level the same logic runs through Higher Level and Standard Level (SL). Every subject carries its own internal assessment with its own criteria: the science IA is a single investigation judged on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation; Mathematics carries the Exploration; Language A carries orals and essays; Business Management at HL carries an extra paper. Families who want all IB and IGCSE subjects covered by one home tutor in Matunga usually discover they need two or three people once HL sciences enter the mix, because HL depth and IA supervision are not the same skill as general subject support.

paragraphs: Matunga sits on the Matunga–Kings Circle corridor and has two stations of its own: Matunga on the Central line and Matunga Road on the Western line, a few minutes apart on foot. That is the practical reason an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Matunga has a wider catchment than the map suggests. The neighbours each behave differently for scheduling. Dadar, one stop south, is the interchange that makes the whole pocket reachable at all, and the Dadar page sets out that scarcity-and-coverage argument in full. Sion, just north on the Central line, brings in the Sion Circle junction and the Eastern Express Highway approach, which is how a tutor driving down from Chembur or Ghatkopar arrives. Wadala, with the Monorail and the Eastern Freeway behind it, is the quick link to the Eastern Suburbs and the reason a Chembur-based tutor can hold a 7pm slot in Matunga at all. Most tutors here treat Matunga, Dadar, Sion and Wadala as one working area and will not go further.

The travel reality is worth stating plainly, because South Mumbai is dense and short in distance but slow in practice. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers about eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, which is why tutors in Mumbai, Maharashtra are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. For Matunga this cuts the right way: the neighbourhood sits at the top of the island, so the signals that punish a Peddar Road run never enter the calculation, and the two railway lines do the work a car cannot.

sections.heading: What do the Don Bosco and JBCN calendars do to a Mumbai family's week?
paragraphs: They set the pressure points, and the two boards do not line up. Don Bosco International School at Matunga runs IB and IGCSE alongside each other, so one campus produces two assessment calendars at once: Cambridge IGCSE candidates in Year 11 working towards the May and June series, and DP2 students working to IB internal deadlines for the same May session. A tutor who has worked with these families knows which fortnight is already full before you describe it.

The Mumbai school year opens in June, and the first weeks lose sessions to the monsoon more often than anyone plans for. October and November are when DP1 internal assessment proposals get written and IGCSE mock preparation starts in earnest. December and January carry the mock series, the Extended Essay final submission and the TOK essay. February is the squeeze: internal assessments across every DP subject cluster into the same few weeks, and an IGCSE coursework component can land next to them. March moves into study leave, then the May examination session. If a family wants weekly help only from January, they have arrived in the hardest month to start.

JBCN International School, Parel is the other campus Matunga families commonly use, and a tutor working across both soon learns the two calendars by heart. To be direct about what naming them means: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel, or any other school mentioned on this page. Naming them is local context, nothing more. What it gives a parent is timing, which is the single most useful thing a Matunga tutor can bring to the first conversation.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or both: which fits a Matunga household?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it is what most Matunga parents are actually asking for. A tutor at the dining table sees the real working, the handwriting, the half-finished past paper and the phone lying face-down beside the notebook. For PYP and MYP students, and for any student who stops working the moment nobody is in the room, home classes beat a screen by a wide margin. Home tuition for DP Physics or IGCSE Chemistry also means the tutor can flip through the student's own folder instead of asking for a photograph of it.

Online earns its place in two specific situations in Mumbai. The first is a scarce HL subject where the only person who has recently taught that component sits in another part of the city, or another city altogether. The second is the fortnight before an exam, when four short screen sessions do more than two long ones and travel time is the thing you cannot afford. The honest trade-off: a screen loses the small corrections a tutor makes by watching a pen move, and it needs a student who will keep the camera on the page rather than on their face.

Hybrid is where most Matunga families end up, and it is a sensible landing point rather than a compromise. One home session a week for the subject that needs supervision, one screen slot for the doubt-clearing subject. IB and IGCSE online tuition in Matunga carries no travel time, which shows up in what it costs, and it survives a monsoon evening when a road run would be cancelled. The pattern that fails is the undefined one, where nobody decides which mode a session is in until that afternoon.

Online: best for scarce HL components and short pre-exam bursts

sections.heading: How is a home tutor checked before they ring your doorbell in Matunga?
paragraphs: Three things are checked before any IB and IGCSE home tutor in Matunga is shown to you: who they are, what they have actually taught, and whether they can teach the component you asked about. Identity and qualification documents are collected and read rather than filed, boards and levels taught are recorded subject by subject, and teaching claims are tested in conversation about assessment rather than about enthusiasm. A tutor who cannot describe how a paper is marked does not get listed for it.

What that process cannot do is judge the fit between one tutor and one teenager, which is why the introductory session exists and why it is diagnostic. A tutor may be entirely genuine about a subject and still be the wrong person for a quiet Year 10 student who needs to be asked questions rather than talked at. Fit shows up in the first forty minutes, and it is the parent in the room, not a verification file, who sees it first.

So check a few things yourself, and do it in the first session rather than in week six. Ask the tutor to mark one of your child's own answers out loud against the mark scheme, because that is the clearest signal of whether they know the board or only the topic. Ask which year they last taught that exact component, and to which board. Ask what homework will come after each session and how you will hear about it. Nothing stops you sitting in on the first fifteen minutes of a home session, and good tutors expect it.

sections.heading: Why a Higher Level specialist in Matunga usually comes off the Dadar interchange
paragraphs: Matunga is a genuine international-board pocket sitting inside a largely CBSE and state-board belt, and that single fact explains most of what parents here experience as odd. The institutions that shaped the neighbourhood's academic culture are long-established CBSE, SSC and ICSE schools, and the local tuition trade grew up around them: Class 10 SSC Mathematics, CBSE Physics, engineering entrance foundation work. Don Bosco International School changed the demand side of this market. It did not change the supply side.

The practical consequence splits in two. For the common requests, IGCSE Mathematics and Physics, MYP subject groups, DP Mathematics at SL, English and Economics, there are people living inside Matunga, Dadar, Sion and Wadala who teach these weekly and can hold a fixed evening slot all year. For a narrow Higher Level ask, Chemistry HL, Physics HL, Analysis and Approaches HL, Visual Arts, Film, or a second language at HL, the pool inside the immediate neighbourhood thins out fast. That tutor is drawn from further along the Central or Western line and arrives through Dadar, whose own page argues that interchange point at length and need not be repeated here.

Three things follow from this, and they are worth acting on rather than discovering in January. Book the scarce HL subject early in the school year, because the person who can teach it has a limited number of weekday evenings and they fill in June and July. Hold a fixed weekly slot once you have them, since a floating slot is the fastest way to lose a tutor who is travelling in from a stop or two away. And accept a hybrid pattern for the scarcest subject if it buys you a genuinely specialist teacher rather than a general one who is simply nearer.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should be seeing process, not grades: homework finished on time, working written out properly, and a student who can say what a question was actually asking before attempting it. At one term you should see marks move on the specific component you targeted, whether that is an IGCSE structured paper or an IA criterion. Across one full exam cycle you should see predicted grades stop surprising you, which is the real test.

We do not guarantee grades, and no tutor who has taught through a May session will claim otherwise. What a tutor genuinely controls is the quality of practice, the accuracy of feedback, and whether a student knows the mark scheme well enough to argue with it. What nobody controls is a subject chosen at the wrong level, a student who will not write anything down, or an IA topic approved three weeks late. Pretending otherwise just moves the disappointment to April.

If nothing is moving after a month, treat that as information rather than a verdict on your child. Ask the tutor for the diagnosis in one sentence: is it content, method, writing speed, or motivation? Those four problems need four different plans, and a tutor who cannot pick one is guessing. If the answer is unconvincing, or the sessions have quietly become homework supervision, ask for a different tutor. A replacement is a scheduling matter, not a complaint, and it does not mean starting the whole search again from nothing.

sections.heading: Getting started with IB and IGCSE home classes in Matunga: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four things make the first conversation useful. The most recent report card. One marked assessment with the teacher's comments still on it, because that tells a tutor more than a paragraph of description ever will. The subject list with HL, SL, Core or Extended written against each one. And two time windows that genuinely work on a weekday, including whether an adult is home during sessions. Parents who send these get a shortlist the same way, usually within a day or two.

The first session is not a lesson plan being delivered at you. The tutor reads the marked work, asks the student to attempt one question cold, and watches how they handle it. Then they say what the next six weeks will cover and what homework will look like. By the end you should know which component is being targeted first and roughly when you will see movement on it. If that conversation does not happen, the match is not working and you should say so early.

On cost, nobody should quote you a number before knowing the request. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Matunga depend on the board, the level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. A DP HL science tutor travelling in from along the line is priced differently from an IGCSE Mathematics tutor who lives near Kings Circle, and a ninety-minute session is not two forty-five-minute ones. Ask what drives the number and you will get a straight answer.

faqs.question: How much does an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Matunga cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anyone quoting one before hearing the request is guessing. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Matunga move with five things: the board, the level, how scarce that subject is locally, how far the tutor travels to reach you, and how long each session runs. A DP Higher Level Chemistry tutor coming in along the Central line sits at one end, an IGCSE Mathematics tutor living near Kings Circle at the other. Online slots carry no travel, which usually shows in the number. Ask what drives the figure rather than asking for an average.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai really handle two children on different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, up to a point. Through MYP and the lower IGCSE years, one capable tutor can carry Mathematics and Sciences across both boards for two siblings, and plenty of Matunga families run exactly that arrangement because Don Bosco International School teaches both pathways in the same building. It stops working at Higher Level and at IGCSE double-award Sciences, where the depth and the internal assessment supervision are specialist work. The usual honest answer is one generalist for the younger child and a subject specialist for the older one.

faqs.question: Will a tutor actually travel to Matunga in the evening peak, and how late can a slot run?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more reliably here than in most of South Mumbai. Matunga has two stations on two different lines, so a tutor coming from Dadar, Sion, Wadala or further along the Central line is not dependent on road traffic at all. Slots from roughly 5pm to 8.30pm on weekdays are the normal range, with later starts possible when a tutor is already teaching one family in the area that evening. What breaks a schedule is not distance but a slot that keeps moving week to week.

faqs.question: We are in an older low-rise building near Kings Circle with a visitor register and no lift. Does that affect anything?
faqs.answer: Only logistics, and they are easy to settle in the first week. Tell us at the matching stage if the building keeps a visitor register or needs a resident to confirm entry, because a standing weekly slot works far better than a tutor being signed in as a new guest every time. Give the tutor a consistent arrival time and name at the gate. Where the household is upstairs with no lift, say so, since it occasionally matters to an older tutor and never matters if mentioned upfront.

faqs.question: My child is at Don Bosco International School. Do tutors here know that calendar?
faqs.answer: Tutors working this pocket generally do, because so much of the international-board demand between Dadar and Sion comes from that one campus. What matters in practice is that they know February is when DP internal assessments pile up, that the IGCSE mock series sits across December and January, and that the Extended Essay deadline does not wait for anyone's mock results. IB Gram is an independent platform and not affiliated with the school. Knowing its calendar is simply local experience, which is the part worth asking a prospective tutor about.

faqs.question: Is IB and IGCSE private tuition in Matunga better one-to-one, or is a small group fine?
faqs.answer: One-to-one is the right default for anything assessed individually, which at these boards means almost everything. An IA, an Extended Essay, a Mathematics Exploration and a Language A oral all need a tutor watching one student's work closely, and group sessions quietly turn into the pace of the fastest person present. Small groups make sense for timed past-paper practice and for two siblings on the same syllabus. They do not make sense for the student who stopped understanding something in Year 9.

faqs.question: Does online tuition genuinely work for a Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: It works well for content and problem-solving, and less well for supervision. A DP Physics HL student who already writes things down and shares work in advance can make strong progress on a screen, and for a scarce HL subject in Mumbai online is often the difference between a specialist and nobody. It works badly for a student who needs someone in the room to keep them honest. Hybrid solves most of this: home sessions for accountability, screen sessions for depth and for the pre-exam weeks.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three or four sessions?
faqs.answer: You say so and we arrange someone else. Three sessions is enough to tell whether a tutor explains in a way your child follows, and there is no benefit in waiting a term to be polite about it. Tell us which part is wrong, the explanation, the pace, the homework, or the fit, because that detail makes the second match far better than the first. You do not re-register, and you do not start the whole search again. Most replacements happen within the same week.

faqs.question: Do you cover Dadar, Sion and Wadala as well, or only Matunga?
faqs.answer: All four, and most tutors treat them as one working area. A parent typing IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Matunga into Google is usually within a short run of a tutor based in Dadar or Sion, and the two railway lines make that commute dependable in a way a road route across Mumbai is not. Wadala connects in through the Monorail and the Eastern Freeway. What we avoid is bringing a tutor from the far Western Suburbs for a weekday evening slot, because that arrangement rarely survives a full term.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 10 and wants to move from Core to Extended Mathematics. Can a home tutor manage that mid-year?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the decision is made this term rather than next. The gap is specific rather than general: algebraic manipulation, functions, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles, and the structured-response style of the Extended papers. A tutor should audit which of those are missing in the first two sessions and then work through them in order, with timed Extended questions from early on rather than at the end. Leave it until the final term of Year 11 and the honest advice is often to stay on Core and protect the grade.

faqs.question: What happens to a session missed because of school exams, illness or a family commitment?
faqs.answer: Tell the tutor as early as you can and it is rescheduled rather than lost. Most tutors here hold one flexible evening a week precisely because Mumbai school calendars generate last-minute clashes, and February will generate several. What causes real problems is a pattern of same-day cancellations, because a tutor travelling in from a stop or two away will eventually give that slot to another family. If exams are going to eat a fortnight, say so in advance and plan the break deliberately.

faqs.question: Parents search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Matunga. How should I actually judge one?
faqs.answer: Judge on evidence of assessment knowledge, not on labels. Ask which year they last taught your child's exact component, and to which board. Ask them to mark one of your child's answers aloud against the mark scheme, and listen to whether they talk about criteria and method marks or only about the topic. Ask what the first six weeks will cover. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents end up recommending is almost always the one who answered those three questions plainly and then did what they said.

You will get a short shortlist rather than a catalogue: tutors who have taught that component and can reach Matunga, Dadar, Sion or Wadala on a weekday evening. Pick one, run the diagnostic session, then settle the weekly slot. IB and IGCSE home tuition in Matunga starts with that one message.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mazgaon
paragraphs: A request from Mazgaon is not the same as a request from Bandra or Powai, and the difference is geographic before it is academic. Mazgaon sits above the docks on the eastern edge of the island, on the Harbour Line, with Dockyard Road as its nearest station and the Mazgaon-Dockyard stretch as the strip a tutor actually has to arrive in. That line runs east and north towards Chembur, Govandi and Mankhurd, which is where a large share of experienced international-board tutors in Mumbai genuinely live. The schools those same Mazgaon children attend sit south and west of the hill: Fort, Babulnath, Colaba. So the first thing a matcher does with a Mazgaon enquiry is accept that the tutor and the school are going to arrive from opposite ends of the city, and plan for it rather than pretend it away.

The process itself is short and we keep it short on purpose. 1. You send the child's year, board, subject list and two or three evening windows that genuinely work rather than the ones that look good on paper. 2. We shortlist tutors who have taught that exact board and level and who can reach Dockyard Road, Byculla or Fort inside a commute they will still accept in July when the rain is in. 3. You speak to the shortlist yourself, usually by phone, and pick one for a first paid session at home. 4. That session happens in your flat with the child's own folder open, and afterwards you tell us whether to continue, adjust the plan or try a different person.

What you give us at step one decides the quality of step two. The single most useful thing a Mazgaon parent can send is the school's assessment calendar, because IB and IGCSE home tuition in Mazgaon is almost always remedial-by-deadline rather than remedial-by-topic: the child is not weak at everything, they are behind on one internally assessed piece with a date on it. The second most useful thing is honesty about the commute. Parents in the area type IB and IGCSE tutors near me Mazgaon into their phone at nine at night, but near me on the Harbour Line and near me by road are two different maps, and we would rather know on day one which one your tutor will be using.

We do not send a tutor on spec and hope the chemistry holds. A match that works is one where the tutor has taught the specific component the child is stuck on, can be in your building at the same time every week without renegotiating, and has read whatever the school has already told you. If any of those three is missing, the arrangement tends to collapse somewhere in the second month, which is worse for the child than never starting.

sections.heading: Which programmes Mazgaon families are choosing between
paragraphs: Mazgaon households using international boards are usually running one of four tracks, and the tutoring needed for each is different enough that getting the label wrong wastes a month. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs from the early years to Year 5 and is inquiry-led with no external examinations, so tutoring here is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud. The IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers Years 6 to 10 and introduces criterion-based assessment, where a child can be strong on Criterion A and weak on Criterion D and see a flat overall grade that explains nothing to the parent. The IB Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year Years 11 and 12 track with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service. IGCSE, typically Years 9 to 11, runs under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel and ends in terminal written papers.

The handover points are where families get hurt. A child moving from MYP Year 10 into DP Year 11 goes from criterion descriptors to a seven-point scale and a far heavier written load in a single summer. A child finishing IGCSE and entering the DP discovers that the IGCSE habit of revising past papers close to the exam does not survive contact with internal assessment deadlines that land in term time. Both of those transitions are the commonest reason a Mazgaon parent starts looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families can actually book on a standing weekly slot, rather than a crash course in March.

Board also changes what you should ask a tutor. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE differ in paper structure, in how coursework is treated and in the tiering rules, so a tutor who says they teach IGCSE should be able to tell you which syllabus codes they have taught and for how many cohorts. On the IB side, a tutor who has only taught SL will struggle with the extra HL content and the heavier assessment objectives, and the gap shows up in the second term, not the first. We match on the programme and the level together, never on the subject name alone.

If you are undecided between boards for a younger child, the honest answer is that the school you can get into usually decides it for you, and the tutoring question is secondary. What a tutor can do is tell you plainly what the workload curve looks like on each track so you are not surprised by it in Year 11.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: the decisions that set two years
paragraphs: Most parents arrive asking for help with a subject. More often the real problem is a choice made eighteen months earlier that nobody revisited. At IGCSE the tiering decision comes first: several Cambridge subjects are offered at Core and Extended, and the Core tier carries a grade ceiling. A child entered at Core because they were shaky in Year 9 can be locked out of the grade a Diploma Programme subject will later want, and by the time that surfaces the entry has usually been made. A good tutor will ask which tier the school has entered the child for before discussing anything else, and will tell you honestly whether a move to Extended is still realistic this cycle.

At the Diploma Programme the equivalent decision is Higher Level versus Standard Level. Three HL subjects carry most of the weight of the two years: more content, more demanding assessment objectives and in several subjects a larger internally assessed task. Families here often pick HL by university prerequisite alone, which is sensible, but then do not budget the hours. A child taking three HL sciences and a demanding Language A is signing up to a workload that no amount of tutoring in March can compress.

Then there are the internal assessments, which are the quiet reason most Mazgaon home tuition starts. Nearly every Diploma subject carries one: the sciences have the scientific investigation, Business Management and Economics have written commentaries, the languages have oral and written tasks, Visual Arts has the comparative study. Each is marked against published criteria by the school and then moderated externally, and each has a word limit the school will enforce before the IB does. Add the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition on top, and a DP1 student has a stack of deadlines that do not appear on any examination timetable.

What this means for choosing an IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents recommend to each other is simple: ask what they have actually marked or supervised, not what they have revised. A tutor who has supervised an internal assessment through drafting, feedback and the academic-honesty declaration is worth more in October than a tutor who is excellent at past papers but has never seen a criterion grid.

sections.heading: What a Mazgaon home tutor also covers: Byculla, Fort and Sewri
paragraphs: Mazgaon is a hill with docks at its foot, in Mumbai, Maharashtra, and its practical catchment for tutoring is tight. A tutor who takes a standing weekly slot here will almost always be covering Byculla to the north, Fort to the south and Sewri along the eastern shore, because those four are within a short enough hop of each other that two sessions can be stacked on the same evening. That stacking is what makes an all IB and IGCSE subjects home tutor in Mazgaon viable at all: a tutor travelling into the area for one lesson a week is making an uneconomic trip, and the arrangement quietly dies. A tutor with a Byculla session at five and a Mazgaon session at seven keeps it for the year.

The travel reality in this part of Mumbai is worth stating plainly because it is counter-intuitive. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Distance on a map tells you almost nothing. For that reason tutors here are usually matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, and when we do reach outside the island it is along the Harbour Line, not across the western spine.

Dockyard Road is the station that makes Mazgaon work. It puts the area on the Harbour Line towards Sewri, Wadala and onwards to Chembur and Govandi, which means a tutor living in the eastern suburbs can arrive without a car and without touching the evening road network at all. Road access from the east exists too, but a tutor who commutes by train is a tutor whose arrival time does not change with the weather, and in June and July that difference decides whether a weekly slot survives. The Western Line at Grant Road and Mumbai Central serves families whose tutor comes from the Churchgate side, and Metro Line 3 has changed what a Cuffe Parade or BKC-based tutor can reasonably offer in the evening.

Within Mazgaon itself the geography does one more thing to your schedule. The climb from the dock road up to the residential slopes is short but steep, and the lanes are narrow and often blocked by dock traffic in the late afternoon. A tutor arriving at Dockyard Road at six is not necessarily at your gate at six, and the honest fix is to set the slot at six thirty rather than argue with it every week.

sections.heading: Why does the school run from Mazgaon go south while the tutors come from the east?
paragraphs: Because the international-board schools Mazgaon families use are not in Mazgaon. Children here travel south and west each morning, most commonly to Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort and to Bombay International School at Babulnath, both of which run IGCSE and the IB Diploma Programme. The tutor supply, meanwhile, comes up the Harbour Line from Chembur, Govandi and Wadala, because that is where tutors can afford to live and where enough teaching work exists to make the rest of their week viable. The school run and the tutor run point in opposite directions, and that is the one fact about tutoring in Mazgaon that is not true of most other Mumbai neighbourhoods.

The consequence is practical. Your best available match is often someone who has never set foot inside your child's school, has not met the subject teacher and does not know the house style of its assessment feedback. That is survivable, but only if the tutor is briefed properly in the first fortnight. Give them the school's term calendar and internal assessment deadline sheet, the last written report with the teacher's comments rather than only the grades, one marked piece of work with the teacher's annotations on it, and the name of the examination series the child is sitting. Those four documents close most of the gap that physical distance from the school creates.

A worked example makes the point. Take a Diploma Programme student at Cathedral and John Connon School writing the History internal assessment, the 2,200-word historical investigation built in three parts: identification and evaluation of sources, the investigation itself, and the reflection. She chooses the 1944 explosion in the docks below her own house, which is a strong local topic with real archival material. Her tutor lives in Chembur and is excellent on the component. What he cannot know unaided is that her school expects the source evaluation to be structured a particular way, that her teacher has already rejected two classmates' question wordings for being too broad, and that the school's internal draft deadline falls a fortnight before the one the student has in her head. Hand him the deadline sheet and the annotated sample and he is immediately as useful as a tutor sitting in the staffroom. Withhold them and he will teach the component correctly and still miss the school.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with Bombay International School, Cathedral and John Connon School or any other school named on this page. We name them because they set the calendar your family lives by, and because the pressure points in a Mumbai international-board year are set by school deadlines long before they are set by examination dates.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in Mazgaon: which one holds for a full term?
paragraphs: Home tuition holds best, and that is why it is what we lead with. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mazgaon who sits at your dining table has the child's folder, the school's printed deadline sheet and the annotated past paper in front of them without anyone having to photograph anything. For younger PYP and MYP children the physical presence also does the work no screen does: it stops the child leaving the table. The cost of home tuition is the commute, which you pay for in one of two ways, either in the fee or in the slot being at the tutor's convenience rather than yours.

Online is the right answer more often than parents expect, and in Mazgaon it is often the only way to reach a genuinely scarce specialist. If your child needs a Theory of Knowledge supervisor or a tutor for a less commonly taught Diploma subject, an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Mazgaon may be sitting in Pune or Chennai, and the alternative is not a better local tutor, it is no tutor. Online works well for essay feedback, for marking against criteria with the script shared on screen, and for short frequent check-ins during a drafting period. It works badly for a child who needs their attention managed, and it works badly for diagram-heavy working unless both sides have a tablet and a stylus.

Hybrid is what most of our Mazgaon families settle into by the second term without ever planning it. One session a week at home, where the longer teaching happens, plus one short online session timed to a draft deadline. The online session is the one that survives the week your child gets home from Fort at seven, the week the tutor's train is held up, and the week before the mid-term break when nobody wants to travel. Treat it as the resilience in the arrangement rather than a downgrade.

One honest trade-off about online that sales pages skip: a tutor who has never been in the room does not notice the things a parent does not report. They do not see that the child is working on a bed with a laptop balanced on a pillow, or that there is a television on. If you go fully online, walk past once a session for the first month and tell the tutor what you saw.

sections.heading: How are tutors checked before they reach your Mazgaon flat?
paragraphs: Every tutor is identity-verified, has their qualifications sighted, and has their board and level experience checked against what they claim before any profile is shown to a parent. We ask which syllabus codes they have taught, for how many cohorts, and whether that teaching was in a school, a centre or privately, because those produce very different tutors. A tutor who has only ever worked one-to-one may be excellent at explaining and weak at predicting what a moderator will penalise. A tutor who has taught in an IB school knows the moderation process from the inside. Neither is automatically better, but you should know which one is coming.

Verification does not end at the profile, which is why we treat the first fortnight as part of the check. You are looking for three things in those first sessions. Does the tutor know the component, not just the subject? Do they teach to the criteria rather than to the topic? And do they arrive at the time they agreed, which in this part of Mumbai is a genuine test of whether they have planned their evening honestly. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Mazgaon families keep for a full year is almost always one who was punctual in week one.

There are checks only you can make, and they matter more than anything we can do from a distance. Ask to see one piece of marked work the tutor has given feedback on, with the student's details removed. Ask directly how many other students they currently teach on a weekday evening, because a tutor with too many is the one who will cancel on you in February. Ask what they will do when the child's school deadline and the tutor's own plan disagree, and listen for whether the school wins. And sit within earshot for the first two sessions, not to supervise but to hear whether the child is talking or only listening.

On access, be explicit early. Most Mazgaon buildings want a name, a photograph and a phone number at the gate before a visitor is let up, and some want it in writing from the flat. Tell us the building's rule when you book and we pass it to the tutor before the first visit, so an IB and IGCSE home teacher in Mazgaon is not standing in the lane at six thirty arguing with a watchman about a lesson you have already paid for.

Tutors state syllabus codes taught and whether in a school, centre or privately

sections.heading: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Mazgaon depend on?
paragraphs: Fees depend on five things, and we will not quote a number before we know all five: the board and level, the subject's scarcity, how far the tutor travels, how long the session runs, and whether the slot is weekly all year or concentrated into an examination run. We do not publish a price list because a published price is always wrong for somebody, and the parents it is most wrong for are the ones with an unusual subject, which in Mazgaon is a large share of them.

Level moves the fee most. A Diploma Programme Higher Level subject costs more per hour than the same subject at IGCSE, because the pool of tutors who have genuinely taught it is smaller and because the preparation behind each session is longer. Scarcity moves it next. Common Diploma sciences and the main language subjects have real competition among tutors in Mumbai and the rate reflects that. A less commonly offered Group 3 or Group 6 subject, or a Theory of Knowledge supervisor, has almost none, and the rate is set by how far the one available person has to come.

Travel is the factor parents in this area underestimate. A tutor coming into Mazgaon from the eastern suburbs on the Harbour Line is spending real time on your lesson before it begins, and if they cannot stack a second session in Byculla, Fort or Sewri on the same trip, that time has to be paid for somewhere. This is also why the same tutor may quote differently for a Tuesday than for a Saturday morning. Session length and frequency work the other way: two ninety-minute sessions a week usually cost less per hour than one ad hoc session booked three days before a deadline, because the tutor can plan around a standing slot.

When parents search for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Mazgaon what they usually mean is the best value, and those are not the same search. The expensive mistake is not paying a high rate for a specialist. It is paying a low rate for twelve weeks of generic subject revision when the child needed six focused sessions on one internally assessed component. Before you compare rates, get clear on which of those two you are buying, and ask every tutor you speak to which one they think they are selling.
bullets: Board and level: a Higher Level Diploma subject sits above the same IGCSE subject
Scarcity: thin tutor pools in less common subjects set their own rate
Travel: an unstacked trip into Mazgaon is time the tutor pays for

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one Mumbai exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not expect a grade change, and anyone who promises one is selling. What you should expect by then is diagnostic clarity: the tutor can tell you in one sentence what is actually wrong, and that sentence should be more specific than weak in the subject. It should sound like she understands the content and loses marks on command terms, or he can do the calculation and cannot write the method down in a way a marker can follow. You should also see the child arriving at sessions with their own questions rather than waiting to be told what to do. If neither of those has happened in four weeks, say so.

At one term, roughly a quarter of the Mumbai school year, you should see movement on the thing you measure. For an IGCSE child that usually means school test marks moving in the right direction and fewer whole topics left blank. For a Diploma Programme child it is more often a completed internal assessment draft submitted on the school's internal deadline rather than the official one, because getting a draft in on time is itself the skill most DP1 students are missing. Marks on a first draft are the wrong thing to look at. Whether the draft existed on the day it was due is the right thing.

At one full examination cycle you can judge the arrangement properly, and only then. A cycle includes the heavy drafting stretch, the mock series and the real papers, and tutoring is only one input into it. Attendance, the school's own teaching, how the child sleeps in April and how many subjects are being carried all matter as much. We do not guarantee grades, and you should be cautious about anyone in Mumbai who does, because no one outside the examination hall controls the outcome.

The honest limits are worth saying out loud. Tutoring cannot fix a subject chosen against a child's strengths, it cannot replace classroom teaching the child is not attending, and it cannot compress two years of Higher Level content into a final term. What it reliably does is convert understanding into marks, keep internally assessed work on schedule, and give a child somewhere to be confused out loud once a week.
bullets: Four weeks: a specific diagnosis, not a grade change
Four weeks: the child brings their own questions to the session
One term: school test marks moving and fewer blank topics
One term: internal assessment drafts arriving on the school's internal deadline
One cycle: judge the arrangement only after mocks and the real papers

sections.heading: Starting home classes in Mazgaon: what to have ready for session one
paragraphs: Have four things on the table before the tutor arrives and the first session is worth double. The school's term calendar and internal assessment deadline sheet. The most recent written report, with the teacher's comments and not only the grades. One recent piece of marked work with the annotations still on it. And the child's own account, in their words, of where it goes wrong, which is frequently different from the school's account and occasionally more accurate. Parents who send these in advance get a first session that teaches. Parents who do not get a first session that interviews.

The first session itself is diagnostic and should feel like it. Expect the tutor to work through a recent script with your child rather than start at the beginning of a chapter, to ask which command terms the child finds ambiguous, and to end by naming two or three specific things to fix and the order to fix them in. They should also tell you what they are not going to cover, because a tutor who claims every weakness is addressable in the same term has not looked at the calendar. By the end of session one you should have a plan with dates on it, not a syllabus.

On logistics, settle the boring details before week two rather than after a problem. Agree a fixed slot and protect it, because a floating slot is the first thing a busy tutor drops. Agree where in the flat the session happens and keep it the same place. Agree what happens to a cancelled session on either side, and agree it in writing in the chat where you booked. Send the building's visitor rule to the tutor. We run all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mazgaon parents book for a full term, and the ones that run smoothly are the ones where these four things were settled on day one.

If you are not sure whether to start now or wait for the next term, start now if there is an internally assessed deadline inside the next eight weeks, and wait if there is not and your child is already carrying a heavy week. Starting badly timed tutoring is a real cost, not a neutral one.

faqs.question: How quickly can you send an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mazgaon?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days for a common subject, and longer for a scarce one. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mazgaon for a mainstream Diploma Programme or IGCSE subject is typically shortlisted inside two or three days, because several suitable tutors already work along the Harbour Line and in Fort. A less commonly taught Group 3 or Group 6 Diploma subject, or a Theory of Knowledge supervisor, can take longer, and we will tell you that honestly rather than send someone unsuitable to meet a deadline. If your need is urgent because of a school deadline, say so in the first message and we will prioritise availability over the perfect profile.

faqs.question: Will a tutor from Chembur or Govandi really travel to Mazgaon on a weekday?
faqs.answer: Yes, and more reliably than a tutor from the western suburbs will. Mazgaon is on the Harbour Line, so Dockyard Road is a direct train from Chembur, Govandi and Wadala, with no road network in between to go wrong. That is why a tutor from the eastern suburbs often turns out to be a better bet here than someone from Worli or Bandra, who would be crossing the slow middle of the island at exactly the wrong hour. The condition is that the slot suits the train, so a tutor who proposes six thirty rather than six is usually being realistic, not awkward.

faqs.question: Our building near Dockyard Road has a strict visitor policy. How is that handled?
faqs.answer: Tell us the rule when you book and we pass it to the tutor before the first visit. Most Mazgaon buildings want a name, a photograph and a phone number logged at the gate, and some want written confirmation from the flat for a recurring visitor. The cleanest arrangement is a standing entry for a fixed weekly slot, which most societies will grant once they have seen the tutor twice. Send the tutor's name to your secretary in the same week you book. The avoidable failure is a tutor waiting in the lane while someone upstairs looks for a phone, which eats a quarter of the session.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to know my child's school to be useful?
faqs.answer: No, but they need the school's paperwork. Because Mazgaon families mostly travel south to Fort and Babulnath for school while tutors come in from the east, your tutor will often never have been inside the building. That gap closes with four documents: the term calendar, the internal assessment deadline sheet, the last written report with comments, and one marked script with the teacher's annotations on it. With those, a tutor who has taught the component knows what the school expects. Without them, even a tutor who lives next door to the school is guessing about your particular teacher.

faqs.question: Why will you not quote a fee before a phone call?
faqs.answer: Because a quote given before we know the subject, level and travel is a guess that someone later has to break. Fees move with board and level, with how scarce that subject's tutors are, with how far the tutor travels into Mazgaon and whether they can stack another session nearby, with session length, and with whether you want a standing weekly slot or a concentrated run before examinations. Two families on the same street can legitimately pay different rates for the same subject if one needs Higher Level and the other Standard Level. One short call gets you a real number instead of a range you cannot plan with.

faqs.question: Does online tuition actually work for IB internal assessments?
faqs.answer: For internal assessments it works well, often better than home sessions. Marking a draft against published criteria is a screen-sharing task: the tutor has the script and the criteria side by side, comments in place, and the child can see exactly which sentence lost the mark. Short frequent online check-ins during a drafting fortnight also beat one long weekly visit. Where online struggles is diagram-heavy working without a stylus, and younger children whose attention needs managing in the room. Most families here end up running the teaching at home and the draft feedback online, which is the sensible split rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we change the tutor. There is no argument and no requirement to justify it at length, though the more specific you are the better the replacement will be. Saying the explanations are too fast, or my daughter is not talking in the sessions, or he keeps teaching topics instead of the coursework, lets us match differently rather than repeat the mistake. A change in the first fortnight costs very little. A change in month four costs a term. Most mismatches are visible by session three, so trust what you have seen rather than waiting to be sure.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask the tutor for the diagnosis in one sentence before you consider changing anyone. At four weeks you should not expect a grade to move, but you should expect the tutor to say precisely what is wrong, in terms more specific than weak in the subject. If they can, the work is probably on track and the marks lag the understanding by a few weeks. If they cannot, that is the real problem and it is a matching problem, not an effort problem. Either way, raise it at four weeks rather than three months, when the examination calendar still leaves room to recover.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children if they are on different boards?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not force it. A tutor comfortable with both IGCSE and the Diploma Programme in the same subject area can run back-to-back sessions in your flat, which saves a commute and usually improves the rate. It stops working when the two children need different subjects, or when one is a young MYP child who needs a very different style from a DP2 sibling. Two shorter sessions on the same evening with one tutor is a real efficiency in Mazgaon, where the commute is the expensive part. Two compromised sessions is not.

faqs.question: Which IB and IGCSE subjects can you cover in Mazgaon?
faqs.answer: Across both boards and all levels, with real differences in how fast we can fill each one. Mainstream IGCSE subjects and the common Diploma Programme sciences, mathematics and language subjects are well covered by tutors living within reach of Mazgaon, Byculla, Fort and Sewri. Group 3 humanities, Group 6 arts, Theory of Knowledge supervision and Extended Essay support draw on a thinner pool, and for those an online specialist from elsewhere is often the honest recommendation. Tell us the subject and level in your first message and we will say plainly which category it falls into.

faqs.question: We get back from Fort late. Can sessions start after eight in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Mazgaon late slots are common precisely because of the school run south. A child leaving Fort or Babulnath at the end of the school day, then doing an activity, is realistically not at their desk before eight. Tutors who work this area plan for it, and a tutor travelling home on the Harbour Line after a late session is usually fine with it. What does not work is a late slot that moves every week. Fix one evening and keep it, and tell the tutor at the booking stage that it will be a late start rather than discovering it in week two.

faqs.question: Do we need a separate study room, or is the dining table acceptable?
faqs.answer: The dining table is fine and often better than a bedroom. What matters is that it is the same place every week, has room for two people and a spread-out folder, has a plug within reach, and is not facing a television. Many Mazgaon flats are older and compact, and tutors who work in South Mumbai are entirely used to that. One thing to get right: sit within earshot for the first couple of sessions. Not to supervise the tutor, but to hear whether your child is talking or only nodding, which tells you more than any report will.

mazgaon.closingCta: Send us your child's year, board, subject list and two evening windows that genuinely work, and tell us which school they travel to and what the next deadline is. We shortlist tutors who have taught that exact board and level and can reach Mazgaon, Byculla, Fort or Sewri reliably. You speak to the shortlist yourself, then run one paid session at home with the child's folder open. If it is not right, say so and we match again.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mira Road
paragraphs: The request we get from Mira Road is different from the one that reaches us from Khar West or Powai or anywhere else in Mumbai. A parent here rarely asks for a tutor three evenings a week, because they already know what their own week looks like: the child leaves for Dahisar East or Borivali before eight in the morning and is back at the society gate somewhere between half past five and seven, depending on how the Western Express Highway behaves. Parents here also type IB and IGCSE tutors near me while standing in Mira Road and get a page full of people based in Andheri. So the first thing we ask for is not a subject list. It is the real arrival time, and which two days of the week are genuinely free.

Then the matching runs in a fixed order. 1. You send the board, the year group, the subjects and the school, plus that arrival time and the mode you think you want. 2. We filter the subject pool twice, once by who can physically reach Mira Road for a repeating slot, which in practice means tutors living between Bhayandar and Kandivali, and once by who teaches that component well online. 3. You get a short list that names the syllabus codes each person has taught and the examination session they last prepared a student for. 4. What that process produces for a family in Mira Road is usually not one person. A Diploma Programme student taking Higher Level Chemistry and Standard Level Economics is served better by a Chemistry specialist at home on a Saturday morning and an Economics specialist online on a Wednesday night than by one generalist doing both at half strength. We will say when a single IB and IGCSE home tutor in Mira Road is the wrong shape for the request, which is most of the time once a child is in the Diploma years.
